# WhatsApp Webhook Override: Route Meta Webhooks Directly to Your Server | Dualhook

Browse Docs

WhatsApp Webhook Override
=========================

How Dualhook uses WhatsApp Webhook Override to route supported customer-path webhooks directly from Meta to your server.

Looking for the high-level overview first? Start with [WhatsApp Webhook](https://dualhook.com/whatsapp-webhook)
 and then return here for the implementation details.

What Webhook Override Is[](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override#what-webhook-override-is)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Webhook Override is Meta's alternate-callback routing for WhatsApp webhook fields. Instead of sending supported webhook fields to the default callback URL on the Meta app, Meta can send them directly to an alternate callback URL configured for a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) or for a specific business phone number.

Dualhook uses this so customer message-path traffic goes from Meta to your endpoint directly. Dualhook is not a message proxy in that flow.

In a healthy Dualhook connection with override active:

*   Meta sends supported customer-path fields to your configured endpoint.
*   Dualhook does not receive, inspect, store, forward, or replay those payloads.
*   Dualhook still receives non-overridable management fields on its app-level callback so it can maintain dashboard state, account alerts, and operational metadata.

This is the core privacy boundary: message content, media metadata, chat history, app echoes, and contact-sync payloads do not pass through Dualhook when override is active.

Routing Priority[](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override#routing-priority)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For a supported webhook field, Meta resolves the destination in this order:

1.  Phone-number-level alternate callback, if configured.
2.  WABA-level alternate callback, if configured.
3.  The default app callback URL, if no alternate callback exists.

Dualhook configures WABA-level routing. Meta supports a phone-number-level override with higher priority, but Dualhook does not create or manage that override.

For webhook fields that do not support override, Meta always sends the webhook to the default app callback URL.

Fields That Can Be Overridden[](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override#fields-that-can-be-overridden)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta's override support applies only to specific webhook field types:

| Field | Typical path in Dualhook |
| --- | --- |
| `messages` | Your endpoint |
| `message_echoes` | Your endpoint |
| `calls` | Your endpoint when calling webhooks are used |
| `consumer_profile` | Your endpoint if subscribed |
| `messaging_handovers` | Your endpoint if subscribed |
| `group_lifecycle_update` | Your endpoint if subscribed |
| `group_participants_update` | Your endpoint if subscribed |
| `group_settings_update` | Your endpoint if subscribed |
| `group_status_update` | Your endpoint if subscribed |
| `smb_message_echoes` | Your endpoint |
| `smb_app_state_sync` | Your endpoint |
| `history` | Your endpoint |
| `account_settings_update` | Your endpoint if subscribed |

The important operational point is that supported fields are not forwarded by Dualhook. Meta chooses the callback target and sends the webhook there directly.

What Stays on Dualhook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override#what-stays-on-dualhook)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Fields that do not support override stay on the app-level callback. Dualhook handles these as operational metadata, not message content.

Examples include:

*   [`message_template_status_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-message-template-status-update)
    
*   [`message_template_quality_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-message-template-quality-update)
    
*   [`message_template_components_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-message-template-components-update)
    
*   [`template_category_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-template-category-update)
    
*   [`account_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-account-update)
    
*   [`account_review_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-account-review-update)
    
*   [`account_alerts`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-account-alerts)
    
*   [`business_capability_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-business-capability-update)
    
*   [`security`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-security)
    

Dualhook may forward normalized management notifications to your configured endpoint and logs delivery metadata for those operational events. It does not store customer message bodies or media.

What Dualhook Configures[](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override#what-dualhook-configures)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

During onboarding, Dualhook collects your webhook endpoint URL and verify token before the Meta Embedded Signup popup opens. After signup completes, Dualhook subscribes the app with that WABA-level override. Meta verifies the endpoint before accepting the configuration.

The verify token is used by Meta's GET challenge when it verifies your endpoint. Dualhook stores it only for configuration and retry purposes.

Every Dualhook connection under the same WABA must therefore use the same webhook URL and verify token. Changing that configuration updates the WABA and its sibling connections together.

Coexistence Syncs[](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override#coexistence-syncs)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For Coexistence connections, Dualhook triggers Meta's one-time `history` and `smb_app_state_sync` sync requests after override is accepted.

Those trigger calls are not the payload delivery path. If the business approved history or contact sharing, Meta sends the resulting `history` and `smb_app_state_sync` webhooks directly to your endpoint through the active override.

A successful trigger only means Meta accepted the request. It does not prove that the business shared history, that Meta generated every chunk, or that your endpoint received and parsed every webhook.

Debugging Routing[](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override#debugging-routing)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The connection **Debug** tab in Dualhook checks the routing signals Meta exposes:

*   WABA-level webhook override from subscribed apps,
*   app-level callback context.

Dualhook reports WABA routing as the connection's routing mode.

If override is active, supported fields should be delivered to your endpoint and should not appear in Dualhook's management-event logs.

If override is not active yet, supported fields can fall back to Dualhook's app-level callback. Dualhook's app callback defensively acknowledges those fallback payloads without processing or storing them. That state usually means setup is incomplete, the endpoint failed verification, or billing paused the connection.

For the event categories Dualhook does handle, see [Webhook Events & Notifications](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-events)
.

# Billing Enforcement | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Billing Enforcement
===================

What happens to Dualhook connections when a subscription ends or a plan limit is exceeded.

Looking for the high-level overview first? Start with [Pricing](https://dualhook.com/pricing)
 and then return here for the implementation details.

Overview[](https://dualhook.com/docs/billing-enforcement#overview)

-------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook uses one connection-routing state for billing entitlement, plan limits, administrator holds, Meta enforcement, and terminal cleanup.

Only active connections and connections in plan-limit grace can use the outbound runtime. A blocked connection still consumes a plan slot but cannot route API requests. A terminating connection no longer consumes a slot.

Reversible billing and plan-limit blocks are connection pauses, not destructive disconnects.

Subscription Status[](https://dualhook.com/docs/billing-enforcement#subscription-status)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook keeps connections usable while a subscription is:

*   active
*   trialing
*   past due while Stripe is still retrying payment
*   scheduled to cancel at the end of its current billing period

Dualhook blocks routing when Stripe reports a non-entitled status such as unpaid, paused, or incomplete and expired. A failed invoice does not start the five-day plan-limit grace period: Stripe's own retry and dunning period applies instead.

Local outbound access is blocked first. Dualhook then attempts to clear the WABA-level [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
 without delaying the local block. If another current connection shares that WABA, Dualhook leaves the WABA callback active because clearing it would also interrupt the sibling connection. The blocked connection still cannot use Dualhook's outbound API.

Plan-Limit Grace[](https://dualhook.com/docs/billing-enforcement#plan-limit-grace)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If a downgrade or other plan change leaves more connections than the plan permits, the deterministic over-limit connections receive five days of grace. They remain usable during that grace period.

After grace expires, those connections become blocked. Upgrading or freeing enough slots releases only the plan-limit hold; unrelated administrator, billing, or Meta holds remain in effect.

What Is Preserved[](https://dualhook.com/docs/billing-enforcement#what-is-preserved)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pausing a connection does **not** wipe its setup.

Dualhook keeps:

*   Connection name and organization link
*   WABA ID and phone number ID
*   Webhook URL and verify token
*   Access token and related configuration
*   Existing `dh_live_...` runtime keys

That means you do **not** need to redo [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup)
 just because billing paused a connection.

How Reactivation Works[](https://dualhook.com/docs/billing-enforcement#how-reactivation-works)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When you subscribe again or move back to a plan with enough capacity, Dualhook attempts to restore the paused connection automatically.

If reactivation succeeds:

*   The stored WABA-level Meta webhook override is restored and read back for verification.
*   The relevant billing or plan-limit hold is released.
*   The existing runtime key becomes usable again.
*   Unrelated holds remain in effect.

Dualhook keeps the connection blocked if Meta rejects restoration or verification. Payment recovery alone does not claim that inbound routing is healthy.

Final Cancellation[](https://dualhook.com/docs/billing-enforcement#final-cancellation)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Scheduling a cancellation does not immediately remove connections. They remain usable through the paid period.

When Stripe sends its final subscription-deleted event, Dualhook starts terminal cleanup. It immediately denies local access and revokes runtime keys, clears the connection's remote override where possible, conditionally unsubscribes the app only when no sibling connection still needs the WABA, erases stored credentials, and removes the connection row. Retryable cleanup progress remains in a credential-free audit record.

Because Meta does not provide a partner-side API to sever every Embedded Signup relationship, customers are also instructed to remove Dualhook under Meta Business Settings → Integrations → Connected apps.

# WhatsApp Pricing Changes 2026: Aug 1 & Oct 1 | Dualhook

Browse Docs

WhatsApp Pricing Changes 2026
=============================

Meta's 2026 WhatsApp pricing changes: Meta Business Agent billing, 1,000 free monthly service messages per number, chargeable service and in-window utility messages, and October rate cards.

Looking for the high-level overview first? Start with [Pricing](https://dualhook.com/pricing)
 and then return here for the implementation details.

Every dated WhatsApp Business Platform pricing change in the second half of 2026, sourced to Meta's own documentation: what changes, when, what it costs, and what you have to change in your code.

_Last verified on 4 September 2026 against Meta's pricing documentation and its 1 September 2026 pricing and billing notice. Re-check the official rate card for your billing currency before committing a budget._

Direct Answer[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#direct-answer)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Three things change on the WhatsApp Business Platform in the second half of 2026, and one structural change has already happened.

On **1 July 2026**, Meta split non-template messages into two categories: **service messages** (powered by a person or a third-party AI) and **Meta Business Agent messages** (powered by Meta's own agent platform). Before that date, every non-template reply was a service message.

On **1 August 2026**, Meta began charging for Meta Business Agent messages on a per-token basis, at one global rate of **2.00 USD per one million tokens**.

On **1 October 2026**, Meta will begin charging for **service messages** and for **utility templates sent inside an open 24-hour customer service window**. Both are free today. Each phone number receives **1,000 free service messages per month**; only its 1,001st service message onward is charged. The allowance refreshes monthly and does not roll over. Paid service messages use the utility and authentication list rate for the recipient's market and have **no volume tiers**.

Also on **1 October 2026**, Meta will update marketing rates in six markets and utility and authentication rates in twelve markets. Nine markets move out of regional "Rest Of" pricing onto standalone utility and authentication rate cards, and receive new authentication-international rates.

The October rate cards are now published. Use the card for your WABA's billing currency and the recipient's country calling code; do not use the examples on this page as a substitute for the official card.

The Four Changes, With Dates[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#the-four-changes-with-dates)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Date | What changes | Status as of 4 Sep 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 July 2026 | Non-template messages split into two categories: service, and Meta Business Agent. No price change on this date. | In effect |
| 1 August 2026 | Meta Business Agent messages charged per token, one global rate | In effect since 12pm PT |
| 8 September 2026 | Credit and debit cards become available for Meta Business Agent billing | Announced |
| 15 September 2026 (target) | Meta Business Agent token-consumption and cost APIs become available | Target date |
| 1 October 2026 | Service messages charged per message after 1,000 free service messages per phone number each month | Scheduled, rates published |
| 1 October 2026 | Utility templates sent inside an open customer service window charged per message | Scheduled, rates published |
| 1 October 2026 | Six marketing-market and twelve utility/authentication-market rate updates; nine utility/authentication markets move out of "Rest Of" regions | Scheduled, rates published |
| October 2026 (date TBC) | Marketing Messages API max-price Open Beta becomes available to all businesses | Announced, exact date TBC |

Why the 1 July 2026 Category Split Matters[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#why-the-1-july-2026-category-split-matters)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Most coverage of these changes starts with the money. It is easier to follow if you start with the taxonomy, because the pricing follows the category.

Meta's own wording, from its non-template messages pricing page:

> Until July 1, 2026: All non-template message responses to users were service messages (`category: service`).

From 1 July 2026 there are two categories of non-template message:

*   **Meta Business Agent messages** — powered by the Meta Business Agent Platform. A new category.
*   **Service messages** — powered by a person, such as a customer service representative, or by a third-party AI solution. Any non-template message that is not powered by Meta Business Agent is a service message.

Two structural constraints follow, and both are worth internalising before reading any rate table:

1.  **Non-template messages can only be sent inside an open 24-hour customer service window**, which opens and resets with each user message. A service message is by definition a reply. You cannot use one to reach out. Any claim that service messages will be charged "regardless of the 24-hour window" is a category error: there is no such thing as a service message outside the window. See [Service Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages)
    .
2.  **Only one charge ever applies per message.** Meta states this explicitly. A non-template message is charged either as a Meta Business Agent message or as a service message, never both. Meta also spells out a corollary that is easy to miss: a non-template message containing promotional content does not additionally incur a marketing template charge.

Change 1: Meta Business Agent Messages, Per Token[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#change-1-meta-business-agent-messages-per-token)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### The rate[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#the-rate)

Meta publishes a single figure, and it is global rather than per-market:

*   **Meter** — per message, based on one per-token charge covering both AI agent processing (token consumption) and message delivery.
*   **Rate** — one global rate of **2.00 USD per 1 million tokens**.
*   **Cache tokens** — Meta does **not** charge for cache tokens. The rate and typical per-message estimate already exclude them.
*   **Typical consumption** — Meta states one message typically consumes **20,000 to 25,000 tokens**, roughly **4 to 5 US cents per message**.
*   **Cost varies with complexity.** Simple responses consume fewer tokens and cost less; complex responses consume more.

Meta's own worked examples:

| Type of interaction | Example user message | Messages to the user | Tokens consumed | Estimated cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Simple inquiry | "At what time do you open?" | 4   | ~80,000 (~20,000 per message) | ~16 to 20 cents |
| Complex interaction | "I'm stuck on step 3 of this assembly, can you walk me through it?" | 10  | ~250,000 (~25,000 per message) | ~40 to 50 cents |

Note carefully that the 4-to-5-cents-per-message figure belongs to **Meta Business Agent messages only**. It is not the service message rate. Several secondary write-ups have carried that number across to service messages, which overstates service message cost by a wide margin in most markets: Meta's own comparison table puts message delivery for Brazil at 0.68 US cents.

### Billing setup and payment methods[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#billing-setup-and-payment-methods)

This is the detail most likely to break a production rollout, and Meta states it as a warning note rather than burying it:

> As of August 1, 2026 at 12pm PT — Meta will begin to charge for Meta Business Agent messages delivered via our API. Meta Business Agent messages will not be delivered if a credit line is _not_ attached to your Business Agent account.

Not "charged later." Not delivered. If you switch Meta Business Agent on without a credit line attached, your replies do not reach the user.

On who this applies to and how billing works, Meta is equally direct:

> Consistent with industry norms, Meta will charge all businesses for Meta Business Agent, including those that access the WhatsApp Business Platform today supported by a Solution Provider(s). Billing for Meta Business Agent will be via monthly invoicing — via a credit line with Meta — with support for credit cards as a payment method in September (target).

Two consequences worth planning around:

*   **Being on a Solution Partner does not exempt you.** Meta charges the business directly for Meta Business Agent even where a Solution Partner handles the rest of the WhatsApp billing relationship.
*   **Getting a credit line is not instant.** If you already have one for ads or messaging, you attach your Business Agent account to it in Billing Hub. If you do not, Meta's wording is that you apply for one in Billing Hub and it is "subject to review and approval by Meta." Start that before you plan a launch date, not after.

Meta's 1 September notice says credit and debit cards become available as a payment method on **8 September 2026**. Until then, the credit-line requirement remains the documented delivery blocker. Meta also targets **15 September 2026** for APIs that report token consumption and costs in near real time.

### Currency[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#currency)

As of 1 July 2026, Meta lists 16 currencies enabled on the WhatsApp Business Platform, and a Meta Business Agent account can be created in one of them. If the account is not in USD, Meta invoices in that currency, converting from the global USD rate using the exchange rate on the day each message was delivered. Businesses whose Sold-To country in Billing Hub is India or Brazil can only choose their respective local currency.

One wrinkle in Meta's own table: the Brazil row lists BRL, but the footnote against it reads "not yet available." So "16 enabled" and "16 selectable today" are not the same set. If you are billing in Brazil, confirm the current position in Billing Hub before assuming you can create the account.

This matters because the Meta Business Agent rate is published as a single global USD figure. Everyone else's invoice is a conversion of it, so a currency move shows up in your costs even when Meta's rate has not changed.

Change 2: Service Messages Become Chargeable[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#change-2-service-messages-become-chargeable)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta's wording:

> Effective October 1, 2026 - Meta will charge on a per-message basis for all **service messages**, consistent with how Meta charges for template messages. These messages have not been charged since November 1, 2024.

The pricing detail, from the same page:

*   **Charge for** — delivered messages, not sent messages.
*   **Meter** — per message.
*   **Rate** — by market, service message rates will be **the same as the rates for utility and authentication messages** in that market.
*   **Free monthly tier** — each phone number gets **1,000 free service messages per month**. The allowance refreshes monthly, does not roll over, and only the 1,001st service message onward is charged.
*   **Volume tiers** — **none.** Meta states it will not offer volume tiers for service messages, while continuing to offer them for utility and authentication messages.
*   **Rate publication** — the rates taking effect on 1 October 2026, including service-message rates, are now published on Meta's pricing page.

The free tier and volume tiers solve different problems. A number sending 100 service messages in a month pays nothing for them; a number sending 100,000 pays the same market list rate for each billable service message after the first 1,000. Unlike utility and authentication templates, service messages do not get progressively cheaper at higher volumes.

Change 3: In-Window Utility Templates Become Chargeable[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#change-3-in-window-utility-templates-become-chargeable)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta's wording:

> Effective October 1, 2026 - Meta will charge on a per-message basis for **utility messages sent in response to users** (within an open 24-hour customer service window). These messages have not been charged since July 1, 2025.

[Utility templates](https://dualhook.com/docs/utility-messages)
 sent **outside** an open window have always been charged and continue to be. What ends on 1 October 2026 is the in-window exemption in place since 1 July 2025.

Practical read: the order confirmation you send while the customer is still chatting with you has been free for fifteen months. From October it costs the same as the one you send the next day.

Change 4: October Rate Card Updates[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#change-4-october-rate-card-updates)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Separately from the category changes, Meta will update marketing rates across six markets and utility and authentication rates across twelve markets on 1 October 2026. Two of the marketing markets and nine of the utility/authentication markets move out of their respective "Rest Of" pricing regions.

The nine newly standalone utility and authentication markets announced in May are:

| Markets | Change to utility and authentication rates | Authentication-international |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bangladesh, Iraq, Nepal, Sri Lanka | Lower | New authentication-international rate, higher than the current regional authentication rate |
| Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Morocco, Oman, Ukraine | Higher | New authentication-international rate, higher than the current regional authentication rate |

Meta's 1 September notice confirms these nine moves and says the October rates are now published. It also confirms new authentication-international rates for all nine newly standalone markets.

Because service message rates will match utility and authentication rates, a market moving onto a standalone rate card on 1 October 2026 changes that market's service message rate on the same day. The two changes compound in those nine markets.

The Complete Billing Matrix[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#the-complete-billing-matrix)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This consolidates Meta's category table, its pricing page, and the free monthly tier announced on 1 September 2026.

| Message type | Sent when | Before 1 Aug 2026 | 1 Aug 2026 | From 1 Oct 2026 (scheduled) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Marketing template | Any time | Charged | Charged | Charged |
| Utility template, outside customer service window | Any time | Charged | Charged | Charged |
| Authentication template | Any time | Charged | Charged | Charged |
| Utility template, inside customer service window | In open CSW | Free (since 1 Jul 2025) | Free | **Charged, per message** |
| Service message (person or third-party AI) | In open CSW | Free (since 1 Nov 2024) | Free | First 1,000 per phone number per month free, then **charged per message with no volume tiers** |
| Meta Business Agent message | In open CSW | Free (test window, 1 to 31 Jul 2026) | **Charged, per token** | Charged, per token |
| Any inbound message from a user | Any time | Not charged | Not charged | Not charged |
| Marketing, utility, authentication or service message inside 72-hour free entry point window | In open FEP | Free | Free | Free |
| Meta Business Agent message inside 72-hour free entry point window | In open FEP | Free | **Charged for token usage** | Charged for token usage |

That last row is the one both the mainstream write-ups and the AI summaries keep getting wrong.

The 72-Hour Free Entry Point Exception[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#the-72-hour-free-entry-point-exception)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A free entry point window opens when a WhatsApp user messages you through a Click to WhatsApp ad or a Facebook Page call-to-action button, from a device running Meta's Android or iOS app (desktop and web are not supported), **and** you respond within 24 hours. The FEP window then runs for 72 hours from the time you responded. Marketing, utility, authentication, and service message delivery is free while it is open; Meta Business Agent token usage is the exception.

Meta's own category table states that marketing, utility, authentication and service messages are all free inside the 72-hour FEP window. It also states, in the same table, that Meta Business Agent messages are **not**.

Meta spells this out:

> The 72-hour free entry point window is unchanged for message delivery. Messages sent within the 72-hour free entry point window, from Click to WhatsApp Ads or Facebook call-to-action buttons, remain free for message delivery. Meta Business Agent messages are still charged for token usage as of August 1, 2026.

The logic is consistent: the FEP waiver covers **message delivery**. Meta Business Agent's charge is a token charge bundling AI processing and delivery, so the waiver does not neutralise it. If your acquisition funnel leans on Click to WhatsApp ads and you route those conversations to Meta Business Agent, the FEP window no longer makes those replies free. It still does if a human or your own AI answers them.

Note also that the customer service window and the FEP window are independent. If the customer service window closes, you can only send template messages, whether or not the FEP window is still open.

Meta's Worked Example: One Charge Becomes Up to Five[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#metas-worked-example-one-charge-becomes-up-to-five)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta publishes a single conversation traced across the three pricing states. It is the clearest illustration available and it comes from the primary source.

The scenario: a business sends a cart abandonment reminder, the user asks two questions answered by Meta Business Agent, the agent hands off to a human rep who answers one more question, and the business sends an order confirmation. All within one hour.

| Sender | Message | Type | Category | Charge as of 1 Aug 2026 | Charge as of 1 Oct 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business | Cart abandonment reminder | Template | Marketing | 1 marketing charge | 1 marketing charge |
| User | "Do you have this in a Small?" |     |     | Opens 24-hour CSW |     |
| Business | Agentic response | Non-template | Meta Business Agent | 1 MBA charge | 1 MBA charge |
| User | "Do you have this in white?" |     |     |     |     |
| Business | Agentic response | Non-template | Meta Business Agent | 1 MBA charge | 1 MBA charge |
| User | "I'm ready to check out, but my card is expired" |     |     |     |     |
| Business | Rep responds | Non-template | Service | No charge | 0 charges while the number is inside its monthly free tier, otherwise 1 service charge |
| Business | Order confirmation | Template | Utility | No charge | 1 utility charge |
|     |     |     | **Total** | **3 charges** | **4 or 5 charges** |

As of 1 July 2026 the same conversation carried exactly one charge. It moves to three from August, then four or five from October depending on whether the phone number has exhausted its 1,000 free monthly service messages.

The behavioural consequence is direct once a phone number has exhausted its free monthly service tier. An agent or bot that splits one answer across four short service messages can produce four charges where one would have done.

What This Will Actually Cost You[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#what-this-will-actually-cost-you)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta has published the October rates. The remaining work is to select the correct billing-currency card, map each recipient country code to its market, and apply the free service-message tier per phone number.

The formula:

    Added monthly cost from 1 October 2026
      = (service messages Meta marks billable after the 1,000-message free tier
          x service rate for each recipient market)
      + (in-window utility templates delivered per month  x  utility rate for that market)

Both inputs are things you can measure today. Neither is something you should estimate.

**An illustration using a rate Meta has published.** In its own cost comparison, Meta uses 0.68 US cents as the message delivery rate for utility and authentication messages to users in Brazil. Assuming one phone number, all service messages go to Brazil, none fall inside a free entry point window, and that rate is the applicable October service rate:

*   10,000 service messages: (10,000 - 1,000 free) x 0.0068 USD = **61.20 USD per month**
*   50,000 service messages: (50,000 - 1,000 free) x 0.0068 USD = **333.20 USD per month**

Do not carry that figure to other markets; use Meta's current rate card for each recipient market.

**Meta's service versus Meta Business Agent comparison**, scaled to 1,000 AI-powered replies to users in Brazil from Meta's earlier 10,000-message example. The table predates the free service-message tier, so its service delivery line is the cost after the free allowance has been exhausted. Third-party AI estimates are Meta's own, based on what it describes as publicly available information and benchmarks:

|     | Service, lower complexity AI | Service, higher complexity AI | Meta Business Agent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AI agent cost | ~2 cents per message | ~9 cents per message | ~4 to 5 cents per message |
| Message delivery | 0.68 cents per message | 0.68 cents per message | included in token charge |
| Total per message | ~2 to 3 cents | ~9 to 10 cents | ~4 to 5 cents |
| Total for 1,000 messages | ~27 USD | ~97 USD | ~40 to 50 USD |

Read that table with its provenance in mind. It is Meta's comparison of Meta's product against third-party alternatives, and the third-party AI cost assumptions are Meta's own. It is not an independent benchmark of what a third-party AI stack costs you. It also does not mean the first 1,000 service messages now incur the displayed delivery charge.

### How to choose the correct market rate[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#how-to-choose-the-correct-market-rate)

Meta charges by the **recipient's country calling code**, not by your company's headquarters, incorporation country, or server location. Look up each recipient market in Meta's current country mapping: some countries have standalone rate cards, while others share a regional "Rest of" rate.

For an international customer base, model traffic by recipient market instead of applying one headquarters-based rate. A weighted forecast across your largest destination countries is more accurate than a single global average, especially because the nine October market changes move in different directions.

Meta publishes rate cards in multiple billing currencies, including USD and EUR. The effective date and monthly volume-tier reset use the WhatsApp Business Account timezone.

For Developers: Detecting the Change in Your Own Data[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#for-developers-detecting-the-change-in-your-own-data)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is the part of the change with an implementation cost, and the part almost no coverage addresses.

### Today: free service messages[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#today-free-service-messages)

The `pricing` object in a status webhook for a non-template message inside the customer service window currently looks like this:

    "pricing": {
      "billable": false,
      "pricing_model": "PMP",
      "type": "free_customer_service",
      "category": "service"
    }

An in-window utility template currently looks like this:

    "pricing": {
      "billable": false,
      "pricing_model": "PMP",
      "type": "free_customer_service",
      "category": "utility"
    }

### From 1 October 2026: billable service messages[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#from-1-october-2026-billable-service-messages)

Meta documents the post-change shape for a billable service message:

    "pricing": {
      "billable": true,
      "pricing_model": "PMP",
      "type": "regular",
      "category": "service"
    }

So the diff to watch for on a service message is `billable` flipping from `false` to `true` and `type` flipping from `free_customer_service` to `regular`. The `category` stays `service`.

That is the billable shape. Meta's 1 September notice does not document the status-webhook shape for service messages covered by the new monthly free tier, so do not assume every service delivery flips to `regular` on 1 October.

**Do not key your cost logic on `category` alone.** If your billing, reporting, or cost-attribution code currently treats `category: "service"` as a synonym for "free", it will silently under-report from 1 October 2026. Key on `billable` and `type`.

Meta has not published the equivalent post-change payload for in-window utility templates. The reasonable expectation is `type` moving from `free_customer_service` to `regular` with `category` remaining `utility`, but that is an inference, not a documented fact. Treat it as an assumption to verify rather than a specification to build against.

Because Dualhook routes message-path webhooks directly from Meta to your endpoint via [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
, the raw `pricing` object arrives at your server unmodified. That is the data your October cost model should be built on — not a provider's summarised view of it.

### Counting service messages before October[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#counting-service-messages-before-october)

You can size your exposure today with the Pricing Analytics API. Query with `pricing_category` set to `SERVICE`:

    {
      "start": "<START_TIMESTAMP>",
      "end": "<END_TIMESTAMP>",
      "phone_number": "<BUSINESS_PHONE_NUMBER>",
      "country": "<COUNTRY_CODE>",
      "pricing_type": "REGULAR",
      "pricing_category": "SERVICE",
      "volume": "<VOLUME>",
      "cost": "<COST>"
    }

Use the returned `volume` to model each phone number and recipient market, then account for the first 1,000 service messages per phone number being free. Rates differ by market, and Meta has not yet documented how a number's free allowance is allocated when it serves multiple markets. Dualhook surfaces the same per-category volume breakdown on each connection's Usage tab.

### Meta Business Agent analytics[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#meta-business-agent-analytics)

Meta targets **15 September 2026** for new APIs that expose Meta Business Agent token consumption and costs across a specified timeframe in near real time. Treat that as a target, not a shipped interface, until the API documentation is live.

### Volume tier webhooks[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#volume-tier-webhooks)

Since 1 October 2025, an [`account_update`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-account-update)
 webhook with `event` set to `VOLUME_BASED_PRICING_TIER_UPDATE` fires when a WABA reaches a new volume tier in a market in a given month. Tiers apply to utility and authentication only, aggregate at business portfolio level across all WABAs, and reset monthly at 00:00 in the WABA's timezone. Service messages will never trigger this, because they have no tiers.

What Coexistence Users Are Not Charged For[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#what-coexistence-users-are-not-charged-for)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If your number runs [Coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
, the October change does not reach messages your team sends from the WhatsApp Business app. Meta states this directly in its Coexistence onboarding documentation:

> After a business customer has been onboarded to Cloud API, messages sent by the business via the WhatsApp Business app will continue to be free, but messages sent via Cloud API will be subject to Cloud API pricing.

Meta is equally explicit that app-sent messages sit outside the window machinery entirely:

> The 24-hour customer service window restriction applies to messages sent via Cloud API. Messages sent from the WhatsApp Business app are not subject to the customer service window and do not create, extend or affect Cloud API conversation windows or Cloud API pricing.

The practical read for a Coexistence deployment: a human replying from the phone is free and always has been, and stays free after 1 October 2026. The same human replying through Cloud API counts as a service message from that date; it uses the number's free monthly allowance, then becomes chargeable. App-sent messages still reach your endpoint as [`smb_message_echoes`](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-smb-message-echoes)
 webhooks, so you can see them, but seeing them is not sending them and carries no charge.

This is worth stating plainly because it is widely reported as an open question. It is not one — Meta answers it on the Coexistence page rather than on the pricing pages, which is why it gets missed.

Three Remaining Questions[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#three-remaining-questions)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Stating these openly is more useful than filling the gaps with confident guesses, and every one is a real question a team will hit while planning.

**1\. Do in-window utility templates start counting toward volume tiers once they are charged?**

Meta's rule today is that only charged messages accrue toward volume tiers, and it explicitly excludes utility templates delivered inside a customer service window and inside a free entry point window. From 1 October 2026, in-window utility templates become charged. Whether they then begin accruing is not addressed in Meta's documentation as of 4 September 2026. If they do, part of the October increase is offset by faster tier progression on utility. **This is an inference and should not be modelled as fact.** Ask Meta or your Solution Provider to confirm.

**2\. How is the free service-message tier represented and allocated?**

The 1 September notice establishes the 1,000-message allowance per phone number, monthly refresh, and no rollover. It does not specify the status-webhook `type` used for a free-tier delivery, whether free entry point deliveries consume the allowance, or how the allowance is allocated when one number serves markets with different rates. Do not build billing logic around an assumed answer.

**3\. Will the October rates hold?**

Meta's pricing calendar permits rate updates on the first day of each quarter only: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October. Rate card updates carry a minimum of one month's advance notice, pricing model add-ons three months, and pricing model changes six months. The next opportunity to change these rates after October is therefore 1 January 2027, with notice.

The EU and EEA AI Providers Wrinkle[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#the-eu-and-eea-ai-providers-wrinkle)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

There is a fourth pricing track running alongside the three above, specific to a class of business rather than a class of message. It matters disproportionately in Europe.

In October 2025 Meta updated its WhatsApp Business Solution Terms to restrict "AI Providers," defined as providers and developers of AI or machine learning technologies where such technology is the primary rather than incidental or ancillary functionality being made available. The terms took effect on 15 October 2025 for new users of the platform and 15 January 2026 for existing ones, with a carve-out permitting such technologies to be made available to WhatsApp users with European Economic Area or Brazil country codes.

Meta then introduced a pricing policy for AI Providers. Per Meta's changelog: effective 16 February 2026, in countries where Meta is legally required to support AI Providers, Meta would charge AI Providers for non-template messages sent to WhatsApp users. Meta subsequently updated that policy: **effective 13 May 2026, Meta will no longer charge AI Providers for non-template messages delivered to users in EU and EEA markets.** Charges for non-template messages delivered to users in Brazil remain in effect.

The backdrop is a European Commission antitrust proceeding, and it has already moved past the stage most coverage stops at. The Commission issued a Statement of Objections on 9 February 2026, saying Meta's policy change appeared at first sight to breach EU competition rules. Then, on **9 June 2026, the Commission imposed interim measures** ordering Meta to restore free access to the WhatsApp Business API for third-party general-purpose AI assistants, on the terms that applied before 15 October 2025, and to keep that access in place until the investigation concludes. Interim measures are rare — this was only the second such order under Regulation 1/2003 since Broadcom in 2019.

So the EU position is not merely that Meta chose to stop charging AI Providers in EU and EEA markets from 13 May 2026; a binding order now requires free access there while the case runs. The underlying investigation is still open, so the final outcome can change again.

Two practical notes. First, this track only applies if Meta classifies you as an AI Provider, which turns on whether AI is your primary product rather than a feature supporting a business use case. A retailer running an AI order-tracking bot is not an AI Provider; a general-purpose assistant distributed over WhatsApp is. Meta reserves that determination to itself. Second, if there is any chance the classification applies to you, this is a question for counsel rather than for a pricing page. Nothing here is legal advice.

What to Do Before 1 October 2026[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#what-to-do-before-1-october-2026)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An ordered list. The first item is the only one that is genuinely urgent.

1.  **Measure service-message volume per phone number and market.** Use the Pricing Analytics API with `pricing_category: "SERVICE"`, broken out by country. Model the 1,000-message free tier per phone number before applying market rates.
2.  **Measure your in-window utility template volume separately.** Same method, different category. Distinct line item, distinct rate.
3.  **Audit your reply granularity.** Count average outbound messages per resolved conversation. After a number uses its monthly allowance, a bot or agent that splits one answer across several bubbles creates several service-message charges. One reply, one message, is then a cost control rather than a style preference.
4.  **Fix your cost-attribution code before the flag flips.** If anything in your stack treats `category: "service"` as free, it will under-report from 1 October. Key on `billable` and `type` instead.
5.  **Check template categorisation.** Sending a transactional confirmation as a marketing template has always cost more; from October, misclassification errors spread across more of your traffic. See [template category updates](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-template-category-update)
    .
6.  **Push volume where tiers still exist.** Utility and authentication templates get volume tiers; service messages never will. Where a use case can legitimately be served by a utility template rather than a free-form reply, the tiered rate may end up cheaper at scale. "Legitimately" is doing work in that sentence — categorisation rules still apply.
7.  **Download the published October rate card for your WABA currency.** Replace any July-rate assumptions and repeat the calculation per recipient market.
8.  **If you plan to use Meta Business Agent, confirm billing first.** Meta's earlier documentation requires an attached credit line for delivery; its 1 September notice says card payments become available on 8 September. Verify that the payment method is active before launch.
9.  **Separate Meta's charges from your platform fees in your model.** They move independently and for different reasons.

Where Dualhook Fits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#where-dualhook-fits)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook is a badged Meta Tech Partner, not a Business Solution Provider. Customers keep their own Meta Business assets and their own billing relationship with Meta, and Dualhook charges a flat platform fee. Dualhook does not resell WhatsApp messaging and does not mark up Meta's messaging charges. See [Dualhook pricing](https://dualhook.com/pricing)
 and the [pricing doc](https://dualhook.com/docs/pricing)
.

The practical consequence for these changes is narrow and worth stating precisely rather than overselling: the October increase lands on your Meta invoice at Meta's published rates, and Dualhook's fee does not move with your message volume. There is no per-message layer on top. What Dualhook does is operational — connection setup through [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-embedded-signup-guide)
, [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
 so message events reach your own endpoint directly, [template management](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
, and [account health monitoring](https://dualhook.com/docs/account-health)
.

**Do not hardcode Meta's rates into billing logic.** They vary by recipient market and category and can change on the first day of any quarter. Pull them from Meta's rate cards and revalidate quarterly.

FAQ[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026#faq)

-------------------------------------------------------------------

**What changed on 1 August 2026?**

Meta began charging for Meta Business Agent messages on a per-token basis, at one global rate of 2.00 USD per million tokens, from 12pm PT. A typical message consumes 20,000 to 25,000 tokens, roughly 4 to 5 US cents. Cache tokens are not charged.

**What changes on 1 October 2026?**

Two things become chargeable that are free today: service messages, meaning free-form replies sent inside the 24-hour customer service window by a person or a third-party AI, and utility templates sent inside that same window. The first 1,000 service messages per phone number remain free each month. Separately, six markets get marketing-rate updates, twelve get utility/authentication-rate updates, and nine of the latter move onto standalone rate cards.

**How much will a WhatsApp service message cost?**

The first 1,000 per phone number each month are free. After that, the price is the published service rate for the recipient's market, which matches that market's utility and authentication list rate. Service messages do not have volume tiers.

**What is the difference between a service message and a Meta Business Agent message?**

Both are non-template replies inside an open customer service window. A Meta Business Agent message is powered by Meta's own agent platform and is charged per token from 1 August 2026. A service message is powered by a person or a third-party AI and will be charged per message from 1 October 2026. Any non-template message not powered by Meta Business Agent is a service message.

**Can one WhatsApp message be charged twice?**

No. Meta states that only one charge applies per message. A non-template message is charged either as a Meta Business Agent message or as a service message, never both. A non-template message containing promotional content does not additionally incur a marketing template charge.

**Are messages inside the 72-hour free entry point window still free?**

For marketing, utility, authentication and service messages, yes. For Meta Business Agent messages, no. Meta states those are still charged for token usage from 1 August 2026, because the free entry point waiver covers message delivery while the Meta Business Agent charge bundles AI processing with delivery.

**How can I pay for Meta Business Agent?**

Meta's launch documentation used monthly invoicing through an attached credit line and warned that messages would not be delivered without one. Its 1 September notice says credit and debit cards become available on 8 September 2026. Confirm the active payment method in Billing Hub before sending; being supported by a Solution Provider does not exempt a business from Meta Business Agent charges.

**Are inbound WhatsApp messages from customers charged?**

No. Messages a user sends to your business are not charged, and they open or reset the 24-hour customer service window.

**Do I need to change my code for the October 2026 pricing change?**

If you attribute costs from delivery status webhooks, yes. The `pricing` object for a service message changes from `billable: false` with `type: "free_customer_service"` to `billable: true` with `type: "regular"`. The `category` remains `service`, so logic keyed on category alone will silently under-report.

**Does switching WhatsApp providers avoid the new charges?**

No. These are Meta's charges, applied at Meta's rates based on the recipient's market and message category. What differs between providers is whether they add a markup on top and how much visibility you get into the underlying charge data.

**How much notice will Meta give for the next change?**

Meta may update pricing only on the first day of a quarter. Its published minimum notice periods are one month for a rate card update, three months for a pricing model add-on, and six months for a pricing model change.

Support, Contact, and Bug Reports
=================================

How to contact Dualhook support, use the in-app support chat, report bugs, attach screenshots or PDFs, and know when email is the right path.

Where to Contact Dualhook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/contact-support#where-to-contact-dualhook)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you are already signed into Dualhook, the default support channel is the in-app support chat in the dashboard. Open the **Support** bubble in the bottom-right corner to start a new conversation or continue an existing one.

This is the fastest way to contact Dualhook about:

*   setup questions
*   webhook and coexistence issues
*   template sync problems
*   billing questions tied to a workspace
*   bug reports and unexpected dashboard behavior

Support conversations are organization-scoped, so the discussion stays attached to the right workspace and connection context.

What the Dashboard Support Chat Is For[](https://dualhook.com/docs/contact-support#what-the-dashboard-support-chat-is-for)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use the dashboard support chat when you want help from the Dualhook team without leaving the product.

Typical examples:

*   "Why is my webhook verified but message events are not arriving?"
*   "Can you check why this connection is showing `LIMITED`?"
*   "The template editor is failing when I upload media."

Each organization can keep multiple support conversations. That makes it easier to separate onboarding questions, billing follow-up, and bug reports into distinct threads.

If you are troubleshooting a live issue, first review [Troubleshooting](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting)
, then run the connection **Debug** tab diagnostics and open a support chat with the exact failing step.

What to Include in a Bug Report[](https://dualhook.com/docs/contact-support#what-to-include-in-a-bug-report)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For the fastest resolution, include:

1.  The affected organization and connection name.
2.  What you expected to happen.
3.  What actually happened.
4.  Exact steps to reproduce the problem.
5.  Approximate time of the issue and your timezone.
6.  Relevant identifiers such as `waba_id`, `phone_number_id`, connection ID, or trace ID if you have them.

If the issue involves webhook delivery, template sync, or health monitoring, linking the report to the relevant docs page can reduce back-and-forth:

*   [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
    
*   [Webhook Events & Notifications](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-events)
    
*   [Maintain Account Health](https://dualhook.com/docs/account-health)
    

Attachments and Response Flow[](https://dualhook.com/docs/contact-support#attachments-and-response-flow)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The support chat supports file attachments for screenshots, exported PDFs, and other supporting material.

Current attachment rules:

*   images: JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP
*   documents: PDF
*   maximum file size: 4.5 MB per file

When you send a new message in support chat, the Dualhook admin side receives an email notification so we can pick it up quickly. Replies appear in the same conversation thread inside your dashboard, and the support bubble shows an unread badge when there is a new response.

For best results, attach:

*   screenshots of the failing UI state
*   PDF exports or incident notes
*   exact error text copied from the dashboard

When to Use Email Instead[](https://dualhook.com/docs/contact-support#when-to-use-email-instead)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use `contact@dualhook.com` instead of the dashboard support chat when:

*   you cannot access the dashboard at all
*   the request is about privacy, GDPR, or a legal matter
*   you need a data deletion request handled
*   you are discussing something that is not tied to a specific Dualhook organization

For privacy and deletion workflows, see [Compliance](https://dualhook.com/docs/compliance)
 and the [Privacy Policy](https://dualhook.com/privacy)
.

# Troubleshooting | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Troubleshooting
===============

Common issues and solutions for Dualhook connections, webhooks, and health monitoring.

Before deeper WhatsApp Cloud API troubleshooting, open the connection's **Health** tab in Dualhook and run diagnostics. It pulls the latest Meta-side health, webhook routing, and account signals for that connection.

Embedded Signup Completes But IDs Are Missing[](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting#embedded-signup-completes-but-ids-are-missing)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If Meta or the WhatsApp Business app shows Dualhook connected but the Connections page is empty, use the dedicated [Connection Not Appearing After Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/connection-not-appearing)
 guide. If Meta shows an error code, use the [Embedded Signup Errors](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors)
 index.

**Likely causes:**

*   Popup `postMessage` did not arrive
*   Access did not include expected business assets

**What to do:**

1.  Retry in a browser profile with popups allowed.
2.  Complete the flow fully without closing early.
3.  Use Dualhook's [fallback discovery](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup)
     and finalize the selected WABA/number.

Webhook Verified But No Message Events Arrive[](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting#webhook-verified-but-no-message-events-arrive)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Likely causes:**

*   [Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
     not active for this connection
*   Wrong endpoint URL or environment
*   [Heartbeat](https://dualhook.com/docs/heartbeat)
     overdue
*   Endpoint returns non-`200` or times out

**What to do:**

1.  Re-check the connection webhook URL and override status in the dashboard.
2.  Send real inbound and outbound tests (not only the synthetic ping).
3.  Check heartbeat status and acknowledge if overdue.
4.  Check server logs for signature, parsing, or timeout errors.

Messages Arrive at Wrong Endpoint[](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting#messages-arrive-at-wrong-endpoint)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Likely causes:**

*   A manually configured phone-level callback taking precedence over Dualhook's WABA callback
*   Legacy configuration still active

**What to do:**

1.  Check whether somebody configured a phone-level callback directly in Meta.
2.  Remove that manual override if Dualhook's WABA callback should be authoritative.
3.  Re-subscribe the WABA intentionally.

See [Webhook Override routing priority](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
 for the precedence rules.

Media Webhooks Arrive But No File Is Available[](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting#media-webhooks-arrive-but-no-file-is-available)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Likely cause:**

*   The webhook contains media metadata and an ID, not the binary file itself.

**What to do:**

1.  Retrieve media using `GET /<MEDIA_ID>` — see [Upload, Retrieve & Delete Media](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-upload)
    .
2.  Download using the returned temporary URL with bearer auth.

Phone Number Stays `PENDING` or Says "Not Linked to Your WhatsApp Account"[](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting#phone-number-stays-pending-or-says-not-linked-to-your-whatsapp-account)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If Meta shows phone status `PENDING`, or the health output includes error `141000` saying the phone number is not linked to your WhatsApp account, the number is usually **ownership-verified but not fully registered for Cloud API sending yet**.

**Likely causes:**

*   SMS or voice OTP verification completed, but Cloud API registration did not.
*   The number was added through an add-new-number flow, which does **not** use the coexistence QR/app-confirmation path.
*   The number was deleted and re-added, and a previous [two-step verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification)
     PIN is still in effect.

**What to do:**

1.  Confirm whether this is [coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
     or an add-new-number Cloud API setup. Existing WhatsApp Business App numbers in coexistence use the QR/app-confirmation flow; add-new-number flows do not.
2.  Check the phone status in WhatsApp Manager or via Graph API. `PENDING` means not fully registered; `CONNECTED` means registration completed.
3.  If phone ownership is not verified yet, request and verify the SMS or voice code first.
4.  Register the phone on Cloud API with `POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/register` and a 6-digit PIN. Meta uses this call to complete registration and enable or confirm two-step verification.
5.  If registration fails because a PIN already exists, use the previous PIN or disable/reset two-step verification in WhatsApp Manager, then retry registration.
6.  If the number came from [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup)
    , complete registration within 14 days. After that window, you may need to rerun Embedded Signup.

**What does not usually block registration by itself:**

*   Display name review still pending
*   Business verification still pending

Those states can limit messaging capacity, but they are separate from the `PENDING` or `141000` registration problem.

Quality Drops to LIMITED or BLOCKED[](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting#quality-drops-to-limited-or-blocked)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**What to do:**

1.  Pause or throttle risky campaigns.
2.  Prioritize utility and authentication traffic.
3.  Review template quality, audience targeting, and opt-out handling.
4.  Resume scale only after sustained quality recovery.

See [Maintain Account Health](https://dualhook.com/docs/account-health)
 for a full incident playbook.

Still Stuck? Contact Dualhook Support[](https://dualhook.com/docs/troubleshooting#still-stuck-contact-dualhook-support)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If the steps above do not resolve the issue, open the in-app support chat from the Dualhook dashboard.

For the fastest triage, include:

*   organization and connection name
*   the exact failing step
*   expected vs actual behavior
*   timestamp and timezone
*   screenshots, exported PDFs, or copied error text

That support path is documented in [Support, Contact, and Bug Reports](https://dualhook.com/docs/contact-support)
.

# Dualhook Support FAQ: Setup, Webhook Routing, Billing and Bug Reports | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Support FAQ
===========

Frequently asked questions about WhatsApp Business Platform and Dualhook.

Answers to the questions Dualhook support gets most often: how to reach us and what to put in a bug report, Coexistence and webhook-routing questions, switching phone numbers, and WhatsApp Business Platform basics. If you are chasing a Meta error code instead, start at the [error reference](https://dualhook.com/docs/api-errors)
.

How Do I Contact Dualhook Support?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#how-do-i-contact-dualhook-support)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you are signed into Dualhook, use the in-app support chat in the dashboard. Open the support bubble in the bottom-right corner to ask a question, continue an existing thread, or start a new conversation for a specific issue.

This is the preferred support path for:

*   onboarding help
*   coexistence and webhook issues
*   dashboard questions
*   billing questions tied to your workspace
*   bug reports

For the full support workflow, see [Support, Contact, and Bug Reports](https://dualhook.com/docs/contact-support)
.

How Do I Report a Bug or Unexpected Behavior?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#how-do-i-report-a-bug-or-unexpected-behavior)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use the dashboard support chat and include:

1.  what you expected
2.  what happened instead
3.  exact steps to reproduce
4.  the affected connection or organization
5.  screenshots, PDFs, or copied error text when available

That gives Dualhook enough context to reproduce and triage the problem quickly.

When Should I Use Email Instead of the Dashboard Chat?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#when-should-i-use-email-instead-of-the-dashboard-chat)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use `contact@dualhook.com` if you cannot access the dashboard, or if the request is about privacy, GDPR, data deletion, or another legal/compliance topic.

What Is the WhatsApp Business Platform?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#what-is-the-whatsapp-business-platform)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

It is Meta's API platform for programmatic WhatsApp messaging. In Dualhook setups, your backend sends through the connection-scoped Dualhook runtime while inbound message webhooks arrive directly from Meta via [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
.

For architecture details, see [About Dualhook](https://dualhook.com/docs/about)
, [Messaging Overview](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-overview)
, and [Messaging Webhook](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-webhook)
.

How Do I Switch to a Different Phone Number?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#how-do-i-switch-to-a-different-phone-number)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use a controlled cutover:

1.  Add and verify the new number in the same [WABA](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
     (or the target WABA).
2.  Register and configure the new sender in your backend.
3.  Subscribe and set [webhook override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
     for the new number/WABA path.
4.  Run test traffic, then move production traffic.
5.  Remove or disable the old number only after the cutover is stable.

What Does My Business Need to Be Approved?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#what-does-my-business-need-to-be-approved)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Baseline requirements usually include:

*   A valid [Meta Business Portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
     and [WABA](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
     setup
*   [Display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
     review and approval
*   Policy-compliant messaging behavior
*   Correct permissions and task scopes for the app or system user

[Business verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)
 is often needed for higher trust, scale, and advanced capabilities.

Which Countries Are Blocked?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#which-countries-are-blocked)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Availability can be restricted by Meta due to legal, sanctions, and policy constraints. Because this list can change, do not hardcode a static country list in operations.

Recommended approach:

*   Validate supportability during onboarding per destination market.
*   Re-check Meta policy and availability guidance before launching in new geographies.

Can I Access User Profile Pictures via API?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#can-i-access-user-profile-pictures-via-api)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

No reliable customer profile-picture API should be assumed for production workflows. Webhook payloads provide identity fields such as `wa_id` and profile name. With Meta's early April 2026 BSUID rollout and later username launch, `wa_id` may be omitted for users who adopt WhatsApp usernames. The new `user_id` (BSUID) field becomes the stable identifier. See the [BSUID transition guide](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-bsuid)
 for details.

Can One API Number Message Another API Number?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/support-faq#can-one-api-number-message-another-api-number)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Do not rely on API-number-to-API-number messaging as a core production pattern. For testing and QA, use standard consumer WhatsApp recipients whenever possible.

# Meta Business Portfolio | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Meta Business Portfolio
=======================

The top-level container for business assets in Meta and why it matters for WhatsApp.

What It Is[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio#what-it-is)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

A Meta Business Portfolio (formerly called Meta Business Manager) is the top-level container for business assets in Meta. For WhatsApp Cloud API, it is the container that owns one or more [WhatsApp Business Accounts (WABAs)](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
.

Why It Matters for Dualhook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio#why-it-matters-for-dualhook)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

To connect WhatsApp assets in Dualhook, your business must have a Meta Business Portfolio. Without it, you cannot complete standard WhatsApp platform onboarding.

Key Concepts[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio#key-concepts)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   A company can have multiple portfolios, but one primary portfolio is usually the cleanest setup.
*   One portfolio can contain multiple WABAs.
*   A portfolio can register up to 20 [phone numbers](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers)
     (subject to Meta policy and account state).
*   Each portfolio has a unique [Business ID](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-id)
    .

Before Creating a New Portfolio[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio#before-creating-a-new-portfolio)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Confirm one does not already exist for your organization.
*   Ensure the user creating it has the correct Meta Business permissions.
*   Use a real business name and business email that match your legal entity details.

Creating duplicate portfolios without a clear reason often causes avoidable ownership and permission problems later.

How to Create a Portfolio[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio#how-to-create-a-portfolio)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Go to `business.facebook.com` and sign in.
2.  Open the business selector (top-left menu).
3.  Click **Create a business portfolio**.
4.  Enter your business name and required contact details.
5.  Complete the email verification flow if prompted.

Creation via Embedded Signup[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio#creation-via-embedded-signup)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A portfolio can also be created during [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup)
, depending on the onboarding path and account state. This is useful when setting up WhatsApp assets directly during integration.

Business Verification[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio#business-verification)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A Business Portfolio can be verified by Meta. Verification can unlock additional capabilities, such as higher messaging capacity and eligibility for [Official Business Account](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account)
 features.

See [Meta Business Verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)
 for details on verification paths.

# Meta Business ID | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Meta Business ID
================

How to find your Meta Business ID and the difference between Business ID and WABA ID.

What It Is[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-id#what-it-is)

--------------------------------------------------------------------

The Meta Business ID is the unique ID of your [Meta Business Portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
. It may also be called:

*   Business Portfolio ID
*   Meta Business Manager ID
*   Business Manager ID
*   FBM ID

Dualhook support may request this ID when troubleshooting account ownership, permissions, or verification issues.

How to Find Your Meta Business ID[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-id#how-to-find-your-meta-business-id)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Sign in to Meta Business Suite.
2.  Open **Settings**.
3.  Go to **Business Info**.
4.  Copy the **Business Portfolio ID** shown near the top of the page.

The Business Portfolio ID is your Meta Business ID.

How to Confirm Which Portfolio Owns a WABA[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-id#how-to-confirm-which-portfolio-owns-a-waba)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In WhatsApp Manager, check the [WABA](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
 details page and verify the owning Business Portfolio name.

**Important:** The ID displayed under a WABA name is typically the `WABA ID`. The `WABA ID` and `Meta Business ID` are different identifiers.

Common Issues[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-id#common-issues)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

### I cannot see any WABAs in this Business Portfolio[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-id#i-cannot-see-any-wabas-in-this-business-portfolio)

Possible reasons:

*   The portfolio has no WABAs yet.
*   You are viewing the wrong Business Portfolio.
*   Your user role does not have admin or full asset access.
*   WABA assets exist but are not shared with your user.

### Can I change my Meta Business ID?[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-id#can-i-change-my-meta-business-id)

No. Meta Business IDs are permanent and cannot be edited.
