# Business Profiles | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Business Profiles
=================

Managing the public-facing WhatsApp business profile for your phone number.

Overview[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#overview)

-----------------------------------------------------------------

The WhatsApp business profile is the public profile data attached to a [phone number](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers)
. This is separate from the [display-name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
 review process, but both are user-facing.

Typical profile fields: `about`, `address`, `description`, `email`, `websites`, `vertical`, and `profile_picture_url` (read/view output).

Dualhook does not currently provide a dedicated business-profile editor UI. Manage fields in WhatsApp Manager or through the connection-scoped [`dh_live_` Runtime API](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api-reference#business-profile)
, which preserves the Meta phone-edge path while keeping the Meta token private.

Prerequisite[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#prerequisite)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

Before updating the profile, make sure the number's [display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
 is approved. If display-name approval is pending or rejected, profile changes can be blocked or delayed.

Field Rules and Limits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#field-rules-and-limits)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   `about`: maximum 139 characters.
*   `description`: maximum 256 characters.
*   `websites`: up to 2 URLs.
*   `vertical`: use a supported Meta category value.

Common `vertical` values include: `AUTO`, `BEAUTY`, `APPAREL`, `EDU`, `ENTERTAIN`, `EVENT_PLAN`, `FINANCE`, `GROCERY`, `GOVT`, `HOTEL`, `HEALTH`, `NONPROFIT`, `PROF_SERVICES`, `RETAIL`, `TRAVEL`, `RESTAURANT`, `NOT_A_BIZ`, `OTHER`.

Reading the Business Profile[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#reading-the-business-profile)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

You can fetch current profile values through the Cloud API for the phone number. Use the profile endpoint for your `phone_number_id` and request the fields you need:

`about,address,description,email,profile_picture_url,websites,vertical`

Updating the Business Profile[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#updating-the-business-profile)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Update requests are partial — send only the fields you want to change.

For a Coexistence connection, update the profile in the WhatsApp Business app. Meta does not support profile updates through the API for that connection mode; Dualhook returns `409` instead of sending an unsupported write.

*   Clear a text field by sending an empty string.
*   Clear websites by sending an empty array (`[]`).
*   Keep payloads minimal to avoid accidental overwrites.

For profile photos, upload media first and obtain a valid `profile_picture_handle`. Use that handle in the business-profile update request. The `profile_picture_url` field is generally a response/read field, not the write field for updates.

Best Practices[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#best-practices)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Keep profile data consistent with your verified business identity.
*   Use a supportable contact email and a stable business website.
*   Avoid frequent unnecessary edits during active review periods.
*   Ensure the profile wording matches your [display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
     and public brand pages.

Troubleshooting[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#troubleshooting)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Update request succeeds but UI does not change immediately[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#update-request-succeeds-but-ui-does-not-change-immediately)

Profile updates can have propagation delay across clients and regions. Recheck in WhatsApp Manager after a short delay.

### Website or email rejected/ignored[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#website-or-email-rejectedignored)

Validate formatting and ensure the value is business-relevant. Remove unsupported characters or malformed URLs.

### Profile picture does not update[](https://dualhook.com/docs/business-profiles#profile-picture-does-not-update)

Confirm you used a valid `profile_picture_handle`. Re-upload media if the handle expired or is invalid.

# Two-Step Verification (2FA) | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Two-Step Verification (2FA)
===========================

Phone-number-level security using a 6-digit PIN for WhatsApp Business Platform.

What It Is[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#what-it-is)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

Two-step verification (2FA) is a [phone-number](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers)
\-level security control for WhatsApp Business Platform. It uses a 6-digit PIN that is required when registering or re-registering a number.

Why It Matters[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#why-it-matters)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If 2FA is enabled, registration-related actions for that number require the PIN. This is especially relevant during migrations between setups, [WABAs](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
, or [Meta Business Portfolios](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
.

Who Can Manage 2FA[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#who-can-manage-2fa)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Only users with sufficient access in the owning Meta Business Portfolio can disable or reconfigure 2FA. When a phone number is registered through Dualhook (via the Register Phone Number action), Dualhook sends the PIN to Meta for that registration request but does not store it. Store the PIN in your own credential manager.

How to Disable 2FA in Meta[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#how-to-disable-2fa-in-meta)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Open **Meta Business Manager** → **WhatsApp Manager**.
2.  Go to **Phone numbers** and select the target number.
3.  Open **Settings** → **Two-step verification**.
4.  Click **Turn off two-step verification**.
5.  Confirm via the email link sent to the business portfolio email address.

After Disabling[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#after-disabling)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Complete the migration or registration task that required 2FA to be disabled.
*   Re-enable 2FA afterward to restore stronger protection on the number.
*   If registering through Dualhook, store the PIN in a secure credential manager with controlled access. Dualhook does not save it for later recovery.

Troubleshooting[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#troubleshooting)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Turn off button is missing[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#turn-off-button-is-missing)

*   Insufficient permissions for the current user.
*   Wrong Business Portfolio or wrong WABA/number selected.

### Confirmation email does not arrive[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#confirmation-email-does-not-arrive)

*   Wrong or outdated portfolio email settings.
*   Email filtering or spam quarantine delays.

### Registration still asks for PIN[](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification#registration-still-asks-for-pin)

*   Disable request not fully completed through email confirmation.
*   Propagation delay after settings change.

# Meta Business Verification for WhatsApp: PLBV vs Standard vs Meta Verified | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Meta Business Verification
==========================

Overview of verification paths: PLBV, Standard, and Meta Verified for Business.

What It Is[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification#what-it-is)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta Business Verification confirms that a business is legitimate inside Meta's ecosystem. Verified status can improve trust, unlock additional platform capabilities, and support growth across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp assets.

Why It Matters[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification#why-it-matters)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Higher trust signal for customers
*   Access to advanced WhatsApp capabilities and scale paths
*   Better eligibility foundation for identity features such as [OBA](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account)
     requests

Verification Paths[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification#verification-paths)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Businesses usually choose one of these paths depending on account state:

*   **Partner-led Business Verification (PLBV)** — WhatsApp-focused, started by a Solution Partner (BSP) during its onboarding. Not offered by Dualhook.
*   **[Standard Business Verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/standard-business-verification)
    ** — all Meta assets, requires website and domain-based email
*   **[Meta Verified for Business](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-verified-for-business)
    ** — paid subscription across eligible assets

[Coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
 caveat: Standard Business Verification is not available for coexistence accounts. Coexistence accounts rely on PLBV through a Solution Partner or on Meta Verified for Business where Meta offers it for the business's country and account; with Dualhook that means Meta Verified for Business, and Dualhook cannot influence eligibility.

Verified Partner vs Verified Business[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification#verified-partner-vs-verified-business)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Searches for a "Facebook verified partner" or "Meta verified partner" usually mix up two unrelated things:

*   **Business verification** is about _your_ business. It confirms your legal entity to Meta and unlocks WhatsApp capabilities on your WABA. That is what the rest of this page covers.
*   **Meta Business Partner** status is about a _vendor_. Companies that pass Meta's partner program review, such as Dualhook as a [Meta Tech Partner](https://dualhook.com/tech-partner)
    , carry a partner badge in Meta's directory. It says the vendor was reviewed, not that any of its customers are verified.

Connecting through a badged partner does not verify your business, and it is not a shortcut around PLBV, Standard Business Verification, or Meta Verified.

Partner-led Business Verification is a service of **Solution Partners (BSPs)**, who start it inside their own onboarding. **Dualhook is a Tech Partner, not a Solution Partner, and does not offer PLBV.** Dualhook customers verify through Standard Business Verification or Meta Verified for Business. Coexistence accounts cannot use the standard path, so Meta Verified for Business is the remaining option where Meta offers it for the business's country and account; eligibility is decided by Meta, not by Dualhook. The evidence Meta asks for is the same on every path.

Comparison[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification#comparison)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Method | Scope | Typical timing | Requirements | Review time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PLBV (Solution Partners only, not Dualhook) | WhatsApp-focused | During BSP onboarding | Legal business docs | Minutes to ~48h |
| Standard | All Meta assets | After portfolio setup | Website + domain email + official docs | Up to 14 business days |
| Meta Verified | Subscription | When eligible | Paid plan + eligible assets + policy checks | ~1–3 business days |

Document Readiness[](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification#document-readiness)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Accepted documents vary by country and region. Before submitting, prepare:

*   Legal business registration proof
*   Address or phone proof matching legal name
*   Consistent business identity across website, email domain, and [Meta portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
     details

# Official Business Account (OBA) | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Official Business Account (OBA)
===============================

The WhatsApp blue checkmark: eligibility, notability requirements, and limitations.

What OBA Is[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#what-oba-is)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An Official Business Account (OBA) is the WhatsApp business account status that shows a blue checkmark next to the [display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
. OBA is granted by Meta for businesses that are authentic and notable.

Coexistence Limitation[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#coexistence-limitation)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

OBA is **not** supported for [Coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
 accounts. If your number is running in Coexistence mode, you cannot use OBA for that number. Evaluate [Meta Verified for Business](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-verified-for-business)
 options instead.

Eligibility Criteria[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#eligibility-criteria)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Before requesting OBA, make sure all of the following are true:

*   Your business complies with WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy.
*   The business is active on WhatsApp Business Platform for at least 30 days.
*   The [business portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
     owning the number is business-verified by Meta.
*   The phone number has [two-step verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification)
     enabled.
*   The [display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
     is approved.
*   The brand is notable (well-known and frequently searched).

Notability: What Meta Looks For[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#notability-what-meta-looks-for)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Notability is about public recognition, not basic account authenticity. Meta reviews external signals such as press coverage from credible publications.

*   Use recent third-party coverage (generally from the last 12 months).
*   Do not rely on your own site, social profiles, paid placements, or sponsored content as primary evidence.
*   Keep your website business details consistent with your display name and company identity.

How to Request OBA[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#how-to-request-oba)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Open **WhatsApp Manager**.
2.  Go to **Account Tools** → **Phone Numbers**.
3.  Select the target number.
4.  Open **Profile**.
5.  Under Official business account, click **Submit request** if available.
6.  Add supporting evidence links and complete the request form.

If the submit button is unavailable or grayed out, the account is currently not eligible.

Denials and Re-Apply Window[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#denials-and-re-apply-window)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If Meta rejects the OBA request, there is no direct appeal path. You can strengthen your public notability signals and submit again after 30 days.

Display Name Changes After Approval[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#display-name-changes-after-approval)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you change the [display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
 after OBA is granted, Meta may reassess the number for notability and compliance. OBA status is not guaranteed to remain after a display-name change.

Cost and Ownership[](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account#cost-and-ownership)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

There is no separate fee to apply for OBA itself. Approval decisions are fully controlled by Meta. Neither Dualhook nor any BSP can guarantee approval.

# WhatsApp Business Phone Numbers: Add, Register, Limits, Remove | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Phone Numbers
=============

Managing phone numbers in WhatsApp Business Platform: adding, removing, and limits.

How WhatsApp Business Platform phone numbers behave when you connect through Dualhook: where to find the `phone_number_id`, how OTP registration and the registered-number cap work, what changes for a [Coexistence](https://dualhook.com/whatsapp-coexistence)
 number, and why removing a number is harder than adding one. The numbers stay in your own Meta assets; Dualhook configures them but never owns them.

Overview[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#overview)

-------------------------------------------------------------

Phone numbers are the sending identity for WhatsApp Business Platform. Each number is linked to a [WABA](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
 and can be used for app, [coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
, and API workflows depending on setup.

*   A phone number can only be actively attached to one WhatsApp business setup at a time.
*   Number ownership, quality, and policy status affect messaging eligibility.
*   In Dualhook, numbers are managed in your own Meta assets — Dualhook does not own your numbers.
*   A connection-scoped `dh_live_...` key can read the selected number's allowlisted identity, quality, status, capability, name-status, messaging limit, and health fields through the [Runtime API](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api-reference#phone-and-waba-health)
    .

Where to Find Phone Numbers in Meta[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#where-to-find-phone-numbers-in-meta)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Open Meta Business settings.
2.  Go to **Accounts** → **WhatsApp Accounts**.
3.  Select your WABA.
4.  Open **WhatsApp Manager** and go to **Phone numbers**.

From this view you can usually see the display phone number, verification and name status, and the `phone_number_id` used for API sending.

Adding a Phone Number[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#adding-a-phone-number)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Common path:

1.  In WhatsApp Manager, open **Phone numbers**.
2.  Click **Add phone number**.
3.  Choose country code and enter the number.
4.  Complete OTP verification (SMS or voice).
5.  Register the phone for Cloud API sending if Meta still shows the number as `PENDING`.
6.  Complete [display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
     review steps if prompted.

**Important:**

*   OTP verification proves you control the phone number, but it does **not** always mean the number is fully registered on WhatsApp Business Platform.
*   In add-new-number Cloud API flows, Meta can leave the number in `PENDING` until registration is completed with `POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/register`.
*   That registration call requires a 6-digit PIN and enables or confirms [two-step verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification)
    .
*   A fully registered Cloud API number should move to `CONNECTED`.
*   This is different from [coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
    , where an existing WhatsApp Business App number follows the QR/app-confirmation flow instead of the add-new-number path.

You can onboard numbers through [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup)
 and then manage them in Dualhook, or add them in Meta first and then connect through Dualhook.

Registered Number Cap[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#registered-number-cap)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

New business portfolios start capped at **2 registered business phone numbers**. The cap automatically increases to **20** when:

*   Your business becomes [verified](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)
    , **or**
*   You reach a messaging limit of 2,000.

When this happens, Meta sends a Business Suite notification and a `business_capability_update` webhook with `max_phone_numbers_per_business` set to your new cap. If you're forwarding management webhooks via Dualhook, you'll see this event flow through.

Toll-Free (1-800) and IVR Numbers[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#toll-free-1-800-and-ivr-numbers)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

You can register a 1-800 or other toll-free number, but the WhatsApp registration call **cannot navigate an IVR**. Numbers behind an IVR system can be registered if they accept calls from international numbers and can redirect Meta's SMS or voice call to a real person or mailbox.

To register a number behind an IVR:

1.  Meta shares 1 or 2 phone numbers that the registration call will originate from.
2.  Allow-list those numbers in your IVR. If you can't allow-list, add the number to your WABA and open a Direct Support ticket asking for the registration-call source numbers.
3.  Redirect the registration call to an employee or mailbox to capture the 6-digit code.
4.  Submit the code via `POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/verify_code` with `code=<CODE>`.

Numbers behind an IVR that can't accept registration calls are not supported.

Identity Change Check[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#identity-change-check)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Optional security feature. When enabled, Meta tells you whether the WhatsApp account behind a customer's phone number has changed since you last messaged them — protecting against recycled-phone-number attacks.

**How it works:**

1.  Enable on the phone number's settings:
    
        POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/settings
    
        { "user_identity_change": { "enable_identity_key_check": true } }
    
    The same safe setting is available at `https://api.dualhook.com/v25.0/<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/settings` with the connection's `dh_live_...` key.
2.  Subsequent inbound message webhooks include the user's `identity_key_hash` in the `contacts` object. Outbound status webhooks include `recipient_identity_key_hash` in the `statuses` object.
3.  Store the hash per customer.
4.  On future sends, include `recipient_identity_key_hash` in the request body. Meta compares it to the customer's current hash:
    *   **Match** → message delivered.
    *   **Mismatch** → message blocked, status webhook with error code `137000` returned.

When you receive a `137000` mismatch, treat the customer's phone number as no longer trusted. Re-verify identity through a non-WhatsApp channel before resending. Send the next message **without** a hash, then capture and store the new hash from the resulting status webhook.

This is the same identity-binding pattern recommended for [authentication-message OTP delivery](https://dualhook.com/docs/authentication-best-practices#identity-hash-binding)
.

    // Send with check
    {
      "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
      "to": "+16505551234",
      "recipient_identity_key_hash": "DF2lS5v2W6x=",
      "type": "text",
      "text": { "body": "Your latest statement is attached." }
    }

Portfolio and Number Limits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#portfolio-and-number-limits)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Portfolio-level number capacity is controlled by Meta account state. In many setups, businesses start with a lower number limit and can increase over time as trust and [verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)
 improve.

*   Keep business verification and policy compliance in good standing.
*   Monitor [quality and messaging limits](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits)
     per number.
*   Do not assume every portfolio has the same number capacity from day one.

Removing a Phone Number[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#removing-a-phone-number)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Before deleting any number:

*   Stop active sends and campaigns that use the number.
*   Disconnect or update any webhook/send logic that points to that number.
*   In Dualhook, disconnect or update the related connection first.

Typical Meta removal flow:

1.  Open **WhatsApp Manager** → **Phone numbers**.
2.  Select the target number.
3.  Use the remove/delete action (trash/bin icon).
4.  Confirm the removal prompt.

**Important:**

*   Deletion can be restricted by permissions, billing/account state, or recent paid usage.
*   Meta may apply cooling periods before some numbers can be removed.
*   Only users with sufficient Business admin permissions can complete deletion.

Common Issues[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#common-issues)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Delete button is missing[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#delete-button-is-missing)

*   Your role lacks admin rights.
*   The number is controlled by another portfolio or partner setup.
*   The number is in a state that blocks removal.

### Number cannot be added[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#number-cannot-be-added)

*   Number is already registered elsewhere.
*   OTP verification failed or timed out.
*   Number format, provider restrictions, or unsupported type.

### Messages fail after number changes[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#messages-fail-after-number-changes)

*   Old `phone_number_id` is still used in sending code.
*   [Webhook routing](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
     still points to the previous setup.

### Number stays `PENDING` after verification[](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers#number-stays-pending-after-verification)

*   OTP verification completed, but Cloud API registration did not.
*   The number still needs `POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/register` with a 6-digit PIN.
*   If the number was deleted and re-added, a previous [two-step verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification)
     PIN may still be required.
*   In [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup)
    , registration must be completed within 14 days or the signup flow may need to be run again.

# Display Names | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Display Names
=============

How display names work, naming rules, review statuses, and common rejection patterns.

Overview[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#overview)

-------------------------------------------------------------

The display name is the business name shown to users in WhatsApp surfaces for your business number. It is reviewed by Meta and must follow naming policy before it is fully approved.

*   Display name and `phone_number_id` are different things.
*   A number can be technically connected while its display name is still under review.

Where to Manage Display Names[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#where-to-manage-display-names)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use Meta WhatsApp Manager for display-name submissions and updates:

1.  Open **WhatsApp Manager**.
2.  Go to **Phone numbers**.
3.  Select the number.
4.  Open the profile/display-name settings.
5.  Submit a new display name or edit an existing one.

Display Name Statuses[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#display-name-statuses)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Typical lifecycle:

*   `PENDING_REVIEW` — submitted and waiting for Meta review.
*   `APPROVED` — accepted and active.
*   `AVAILABLE_WITHOUT_REVIEW` — ready to use without a separate review step.
*   `REJECTED` / `DECLINED` — not accepted; update and resubmit.
*   `NON_EXISTS` — no submitted display-name review record is available yet.

You can monitor relevant management events and logs in Dualhook. Source-of-truth review decisions still come from Meta.

Naming Rules[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#naming-rules)

---------------------------------------------------------------------

Use a name that clearly identifies your real business. Recommended checklist before submitting:

*   Match your legal or commonly used brand identity.
*   Keep formatting natural — no spammy capitalization, symbols, or decorative text.
*   Avoid generic names that do not identify a specific business.
*   Ensure your public web presence (domain, site, social pages) supports the same brand name.
*   If operating under a sub-brand, make the relationship to the parent business clear.

How Often You Can Change[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#how-often-you-can-change)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

After a number is registered, display-name changes are limited to one change every 30 days per number. If Meta updates this policy for your account, follow the latest rule shown in WhatsApp Manager.

Why Display Names Get Rejected[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#why-display-names-get-rejected)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Common rejection patterns:

*   Name does not match business identity evidence.
*   Name is overly generic or misleading.
*   Name includes disallowed formatting or promotional styling.
*   Supporting business information is incomplete or inconsistent.

Troubleshooting[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#troubleshooting)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Status stays pending for too long[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#status-stays-pending-for-too-long)

*   For coexistence / Embedded Signup numbers, `name_status = NON_EXISTS` together with `new_name_status = PENDING_REVIEW` can be an expected holding state until paid Meta verification is completed. By itself, that pattern is not a blocker.
*   Verify business information is complete in your [Meta Business Portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
    .
*   Confirm the submitted name matches your public-facing brand assets.
*   Avoid repeated edits while a review is still in progress.

### Name approved but not visible everywhere[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#name-approved-but-not-visible-everywhere)

*   Client-side propagation can take time across regions and devices.
*   Recheck after a propagation delay and verify you are viewing the correct number/account.

### `NON_EXISTS` appears[](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names#non_exists-appears)

*   On non-coexistence setups, `NON_EXISTS` usually means no valid display-name submission is currently attached to that number.
*   On coexistence setups, `NON_EXISTS` can also appear together with `new_name_status = PENDING_REVIEW` as an expected holding state rather than a missing submission, especially before paid Meta verification is completed.
*   Reopen the number profile in WhatsApp Manager and resubmit only when the account context and current setup path indicate the submission is actually missing or invalid.

# WhatsApp Business Accounts | Dualhook

Browse Docs

WhatsApp Business Accounts
==========================

What a WABA is, how it relates to phone numbers, and how ownership works.

Looking for the high-level overview first? Start with [WhatsApp Business API](https://dualhook.com/whatsapp-business-api)
 and then return here for the implementation details.

What a WABA Is[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts#what-a-waba-is)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) is the top-level WhatsApp container inside a [Meta Business Portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
. It groups WhatsApp assets such as:

*   [Phone numbers](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers)
    
*   [Message templates](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
    
*   Webhook subscriptions and messaging-related configuration

In practice, a WABA is the business object your integration targets for setup and management operations.

WABA ID[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts#waba-id)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each WABA has a unique `waba_id`. You use this ID for account-level actions, for example:

*   App subscription setup (`/subscribed_apps`)
*   Account-level webhook and management operations

WABA vs Phone Number ID[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts#waba-vs-phone-number-id)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   `waba_id` identifies the WhatsApp Business Account container.
*   `phone_number_id` identifies a specific sending number inside that WABA.

Both IDs are required in production integrations, but for different API operations.

Ownership Model[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts#ownership-model)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

WABAs are owned by a Meta Business Portfolio. A business can have multiple WABAs, and each WABA can contain multiple phone numbers, subject to Meta limits and account state.

In Dualhook:

*   You keep ownership of your WABAs and numbers in your own Meta assets.
*   Dualhook configures [coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
     and [webhook routing](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
     against those assets.
*   Dualhook does not become legal owner of your WABA.
*   A connection-scoped `dh_live_...` key can read a safe allowlist of WABA identity, review, verification, health, messaging-limit, timezone, currency, and template-namespace fields. It cannot enumerate other WABAs or expose owner/funding data. See the [Runtime API reference](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api-reference#phone-and-waba-health)
    .

Creating a WABA[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts#creating-a-waba)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Common onboarding paths:

1.  Create or use an existing [Meta Business Portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
    .
2.  Complete required [business verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)
     steps when applicable.
3.  Create the WABA during [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup)
     or via Meta business tooling.
4.  Add and verify phone numbers under the WABA.

For Dualhook customers, Embedded Signup is the standard path because it automates ID discovery and routing setup.

Access and Permissions[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts#access-and-permissions)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

WABA management depends on Meta roles and task permissions. Without sufficient permissions, users may be unable to:

*   View WABA details
*   Manage phone numbers
*   Update templates
*   Configure webhook subscriptions

If something appears missing in UI or API, verify you are in the correct Business Portfolio and that user/system access includes WABA-level permissions.

See [WhatsApp Business API Permissions](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-api-permissions)
 for Dualhook-specific access requirements.

Migration and Portability[](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts#migration-and-portability)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Before moving numbers or changing providers:

*   Confirm whether the target flow supports number migration for your current account state.
*   Review template and webhook impacts before cutover.
*   Keep the same ownership context where possible to reduce approval and permission friction.

Treat WABA/number migration as a controlled project, not a same-day toggle.

# Leave a WhatsApp BSP & Own Your WABA (2026) | Dualhook

Browse Docs

How to Leave Your WhatsApp BSP and Own Your WABA
================================================

Migrate a WhatsApp business phone number away from a Solution Partner: what Meta preserves, what resets, the prerequisites, billing during migration, and the Coexistence caveat.

Looking for the high-level overview first? Start with [Dualhook vs BSPs](https://dualhook.com/compare/dualhook-vs-bsp)
 and then return here for the implementation details.

A vendor-neutral guide to migrating a WhatsApp business phone number away from a Business Solution Provider: what Meta preserves, what it does not, the prerequisites that block the flow, who pays for messages mid-migration, and how to decide whether owning your own WhatsApp Business Account is actually the right call.

_Verified against Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform documentation on 14 August 2026._

Direct Answer[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#direct-answer)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**You can move your WhatsApp business phone number away from a Business Solution Provider — now called a Solution Partner — without changing the number and without losing your display name, quality rating, messaging limits, Official Business Account status, or eligible approved high-quality templates.**

Meta migrates the number between WhatsApp Business Accounts, normally through [Embedded Signup](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-embedded-signup-guide)
 run by the new provider. The prerequisites that trip people up are: two-step verification must be disabled on the number, the display name must be approved with no pending change request, the WABA must be approved with a valid payment method attached, and the Meta Business Account must be verified.

Once you own your WABA and connect through a provider that does not extend a Solution Partner credit line, you attach your own payment method and Meta bills its messaging charges directly to you. A software provider can still charge a separate usage-based platform fee, so verify both Meta's invoice and the provider's price sheet.

Why Businesses Leave a BSP[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#why-businesses-leave-a-bsp)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Two reasons dominate, and they are genuinely different problems with different solutions.

**Cost.** A Solution Partner can extend a line of credit and directly invoice clients for WhatsApp Business Platform services. A provider acting only as a Tech Provider or Tech Partner does not extend that Solution Partner credit line: the client attaches its own payment method and Meta bills its messaging charges directly. This removes a reseller from Meta's billing path, but it does not prevent the software provider from charging a separate platform or usage fee. Compare both layers.

**Data exposure and control.** A traditional BSP or inbox platform usually sits in the message path, because that is what makes an inbox, a broadcast tool, or a CRM sync possible. Every message you send and receive transits — and is often stored on — the vendor's systems. If your objection is "we do not want a third party holding our customer conversations," the fix is not a cheaper BSP, it is an architecture where message-path webhooks go from Meta to your own endpoint. See [WhatsApp API Privacy](https://dualhook.com/whatsapp-api-privacy)
 and [GDPR and EU Compliance](https://dualhook.com/whatsapp-gdpr-eu)
.

There is a third, quieter reason: **lock-in anxiety**. Businesses discover mid-contract that they do not own the WABA their number lives on, and that a routine action — disabling two-step verification — requires the cooperation of the vendor they are trying to leave.

Leaving is a legitimate, Meta-supported operation. Nothing below is a workaround.

What You Keep[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#what-you-keep)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

From Meta's Solution Partner migration documentation, verbatim:

> Clients can migrate their business phone numbers between WhatsApp Business Accounts (WABAs) and retain their display names, quality ratings, template messaging limits, Official Business Account statuses, and approved, high-quality templates.

And on why:

> Since the client's business phone number is not changing, its display name, quality rating, messaging limit, and Official Business Account status are all preserved.

On templates:

> Templates are automatically duplicated in the destination WABA and initially granted the same status as their source counterparts. After duplication however, templates are re-checked to ensure they are correctly categorized according to our guidelines. This may result in some duplicated templates having their status set to REJECTED. Only templates with both a status of APPROVED and quality\_score of GREEN are eligible for duplication.

In practice that means the assets you spent months earning — your [display name](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)
, your [quality rating](https://dualhook.com/docs/health-monitoring)
, your [messaging tier](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits)
, your [OBA badge](https://dualhook.com/docs/official-business-account)
 — survive the move intact.

What You Do Not Keep[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#what-you-do-not-keep)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is the half most migration guides skip.

**Template quality ratings.** Meta, verbatim: "Quality ratings of templates will NOT be migrated. All migrated templates will start with an UNKNOWN rating. This rating will remain for the first 24 hours, after which a new rating will be generated if sufficient data is available."

**Non-approved or non-GREEN templates.** Only templates that are both `APPROVED` and `GREEN` are eligible for duplication. A YELLOW template, a paused template, a pending template, or a rejected one does not come across. Recreate and resubmit them.

**Templates beyond the destination limit.** If the destination WABA hits its template limit during duplication, the remainder are simply not created. Count your templates before you start.

**Duplicated templates that fail recategorization.** Meta re-checks category correctness on duplication. A utility template that was quietly miscategorized in the source WABA can arrive as `REJECTED`. See [template category updates](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-template-category-update)
.

**Message history and media.** Meta's migration page states that uploaded media can continue to be used, but it does not include chat history among the assets it promises to transfer. Treat chat-history transfer as **not provided unless your source and destination providers explicitly document it for your path**, and export anything you need before you start. This matters especially when your current BSP is also your inbox: that product's conversation archive is separate from the WABA migration.

Prerequisites Checklist[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#prerequisites-checklist)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

From Meta's migration documentation. Every one of these blocks the flow if unmet:

| Requirement | Who can satisfy it |
| --- | --- |
| The Meta Business Account has a **verified** status | You, via Meta Business Verification |
| The existing WABA has a status of **approved** | Existing WABA owner |
| The existing WABA has a **valid payment method** attached in Payment Settings | Whoever owns the WABA |
| The business phone number has **two-step verification disabled** | You if you own the WABA; otherwise your current Solution Partner |
| The business phone number has an **approved display name** (`name_status` is `APPROVED`) | You, before starting |
| **No pending display name change request** on the number | You, before starting |
| The number will be registered for **Cloud API** | Migrated numbers can only use Cloud API |
| The number is **not a Meta test number** | Test business phone numbers cannot be migrated |

Meta's first migration step is explicit: migration cannot complete until two-step verification is disabled on the number.

That single line is the whole negotiation. If you do not own your WABA, you need your current provider to perform an action whose only purpose is to let you leave. Ask for it in writing, early, with a date. It is a routine request and most providers action it, but it is not instant, and it is the step that turns a two-day migration into a two-week one.

See [Two-Step Verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification)
 for where the setting lives once you own the WABA.

Billing During Migration[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#billing-during-migration)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta, verbatim:

> Messages delivered before migration is complete are charged to the old Solution Partner. Undelivered messages sent before migration is complete will be charged to the old Solution Partner if they are delivered after migration is complete. Messages delivered after migration is complete are charged to the business customer.

This is not a simple delivery-time cut. Messages delivered before completion go to the old Solution Partner, and Meta applies a carryover rule to messages **sent before completion but delivered afterwards**: those also go to the old Solution Partner. Messages sent and delivered after completion go to the business customer.

Meta also notes that phone number registration happens instantly, so sending and receiving continue without interruption, while template duplication takes time. If template downtime is your concern, migrate templates first.

The Coexistence Caveat[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#the-coexistence-caveat)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If your number runs [WhatsApp Coexistence](https://dualhook.com/docs/coexistence)
 — the WhatsApp Business app and Cloud API on the same number — leaving a partner is more constrained than the standard migration path.

Meta's Coexistence onboarding documentation states that a business that previously worked with a partner and still shares that partner's credit line may see an error when switching to a new partner, and links to a resolution guide.

Do not assume the standard WABA-to-WABA migration path applies unchanged to Coexistence. Provider guidance differs: for example, 360dialog states that Coexistence numbers cannot be migrated between WABAs and describes a provider switch as an in-app disconnect followed by Coexistence re-onboarding. That is provider-specific guidance, not a universal Meta guarantee. Confirm the source WABA, destination WABA, and credit-line state with both providers before choosing a path.

In the field, the way this surfaces is Embedded Signup failing with `#2655093` — the account is still shared with a partner — before the new provider is granted any access at all. That code is widely reported and is documented at [Error 2655093](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-error-2655093)
, though it does not appear in Meta's public Cloud API error tables. The business can disconnect the current Business Platform relationship in the WhatsApp Business app; the previous provider may also need to complete backend offboarding, and Meta support may be needed for a stale relationship. The new provider cannot inspect or remove it before Meta grants access.

The practical consequence: if you are on Coexistence, get written confirmation of full backend offboarding from your current provider, not just "we removed you from our dashboard." Those are different operations and only one of them unblocks you.

Migration Runbook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#migration-runbook)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  **Confirm the prerequisites.** Meta Business Account verified, WABA approved, valid payment method attached, display name approved with no pending change request.
2.  **Get two-step verification disabled.** Do it yourself in WhatsApp Manager if you own the WABA. Otherwise request it from your current Solution Partner in writing, with a target date.
3.  **Export everything you want to keep.** Message history, media, template content, contact lists, and any reporting that lives only in your current vendor's dashboard. Meta does not promise chat-history transfer in its migration documentation.
4.  **Inventory your templates.** Note which are `APPROVED` and `GREEN` — only those duplicate. Everything else is a recreate-and-resubmit task on the far side.
5.  **Complete Embedded Signup with the new provider.** Depending on the migration path, create or select the destination WABA under your business portfolio, then migrate the number. Registration is instant, so messaging continues.
6.  **Re-verify what carried over.** Display name, quality rating, messaging limit, and OBA status should be intact. Template quality ratings will read `UNKNOWN` for roughly the first 24 hours.
7.  **Reconfigure webhooks.** If you want message-path webhooks delivered to your own endpoint rather than a vendor's, set the WABA-level [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
     at this step. Your endpoint must already answer Meta's `hub.challenge` verification.
8.  **Recreate the templates that did not duplicate.** Non-approved, non-GREEN, over-limit, or recategorized-to-rejected.
9.  **Reconcile the final invoice.** Messages delivered before completion, plus messages sent before completion but delivered later, belong to the old partner. Messages sent and delivered after completion belong to the business customer.

Decision Framework: BSP vs Owning Your WABA[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#decision-framework-bsp-vs-owning-your-waba)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Question | Lean toward a Solution Partner / BSP | Lean toward owning your WABA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Do you need a Meta line of credit because you cannot attach your own payment method? | Yes | No  |
| Do you want a turnkey inbox, CRM, or campaign UI included? | Yes | No, you run your own backend or a separate tool |
| Do you accept a provider reselling Meta's messaging charges? | Yes | No, you want Meta to bill its charges directly |
| Does message content need to stay out of a vendor's store? | Not a priority | Priority |
| Do you have engineering capacity, in-house or partnered? | Limited | Available |
| Are you sending high volume where a few cents per message compounds? | Volume is modest | Yes |
| What support and escalation path do you need? | Confirm the BSP's included support | Confirm the Tech Partner's scope and Meta support available to your business |

There is no universally correct answer here. A ten-person company with no developers and 2,000 messages a month may be well served by a BSP inbox. A company sending 500,000 utility templates a month, with a backend team and a compliance requirement, should compare the total provider fee and architecture rather than paying for a bundled UI it does not use.

What Changes Operationally After You Leave[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#what-changes-operationally-after-you-leave)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Owning your WABA moves work onto your side of the line. Plan for it:

*   **Billing.** You attach a payment method to your own WABA and Meta invoices you directly. Watch for [error 131042](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-error-131042)
     if payment setup is incomplete.
*   **Quality and limits.** [Account health](https://dualhook.com/docs/account-health)
     is yours to monitor. No one else gets the alert first.
*   **Template lifecycle.** Approvals, rejections, quality drops, and category changes arrive as [webhooks](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-message-template-status-update)
     you need to handle or a dashboard you need to watch.
*   **Webhook delivery.** Your endpoint's uptime is now part of your messaging reliability. Meta retries, but not forever.
*   **Support.** Support scope and Meta escalation access vary by provider and partner status. Confirm ownership for onboarding, account restrictions, billing, and migration cases before you leave.
*   **Pricing changes.** They land on your invoice at Meta's rates. See [WhatsApp Pricing Changes 2026](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026)
     for what is scheduled.

None of that is hard. It is just no longer someone else's problem.

Where Dualhook Fits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#where-dualhook-fits)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook is a badged Meta Tech Partner, not a BSP. Customers keep their own Meta Business assets and their own billing relationship with Meta, and Dualhook charges a flat platform fee with no per-message component. Dualhook configures the connection through Embedded Signup and sets a WABA-level Webhook Override so message-path webhooks route directly from Meta to your endpoint, and it does not store message content.

If you are leaving a BSP specifically to stop paying per-message markup and to keep customer conversations out of a vendor's store, that is the model Dualhook is built for. If what you actually want is a hosted inbox with agents, tags, and campaign tooling, a BSP is a better fit and you should stay with one.

See [Dualhook vs BSPs](https://dualhook.com/compare/dualhook-vs-bsp)
, [Tech Partner](https://dualhook.com/tech-partner)
, and [Pricing](https://dualhook.com/pricing)
.

_Operational, not legal, advice. If GDPR, data residency, or your current contract's termination and data-return clauses matter to your situation, take your own legal advice and read the contract before you start._

FAQ[](https://dualhook.com/docs/leave-whatsapp-bsp-own-your-waba#faq)

----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Will I lose my WhatsApp number when I leave my BSP?**

No. Migration moves the number between WhatsApp Business Accounts. The number itself does not change, and Meta registers it on the destination WABA instantly so messaging continues.

**Will my quality rating and messaging limits reset?**

No. Meta preserves the phone number's display name, quality rating, messaging limit, and Official Business Account status, because the number itself is not changing. Template quality ratings are the exception: they reset to UNKNOWN for the first 24 hours after duplication, then regenerate if there is enough data.

**Do my templates come with me?**

Only templates that are both APPROVED and GREEN are duplicated into the destination WABA. Meta re-checks category correctness after duplication, so some can arrive REJECTED. Anything not approved, not GREEN, or over the destination WABA's template limit must be recreated and resubmitted.

**Do I need my current provider's cooperation to leave?**

For at least one step, usually yes. Two-step verification must be disabled on the number before migration can complete. If you own the WABA you can do that yourself in WhatsApp Manager; if your Solution Partner owns it, only they can.

**Is there downtime during migration?**

Phone number registration is instant, so sending and receiving continue. Template duplication takes time, so migrate templates first if template downtime matters to you.

**Who pays for messages sent during the migration?**

Messages delivered before migration completes are charged to the old Solution Partner. Meta also charges messages sent before completion to the old partner when they are delivered afterwards. Messages sent and delivered after completion are charged to the business customer.

**Does my message history come with me?**

Do not assume it does. Meta's migration documentation says uploaded media remains usable but does not promise chat-history transfer. Export anything you need before starting, especially when your BSP also provides the inbox where that history is stored.

**Can I migrate a Coexistence number to a new provider?**

It is more constrained than a standard migration. Meta warns that a prior shared credit line can block a partner switch, and provider-specific WABA rules differ. Confirm the source and destination WABA path with both providers, disconnect the old Business Platform relationship as instructed, and get written confirmation of full backend offboarding.

**What is the difference between a Solution Partner and a Tech Provider?**

A Solution Partner (the role formerly called BSP) can extend a Meta line of credit and invoice you for WhatsApp messaging. A provider acting only as a Tech Provider or Tech Partner does not extend that credit line, so you attach your own payment method and Meta bills its messaging charges directly. The provider can still charge a separate platform or usage fee.

*   Meta, [Migrating a client off a Multi-Partner Solution](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/support/migrating-customers-off-solutions-via-embedded-signup)

# Runtime API | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Runtime API
===========

Use, protect, rotate, and scope dh\_live\_ keys for Dualhook's allowlisted Graph-compatible WhatsApp runtime.

Graph-Compatible Runtime[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#graph-compatible-runtime)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Runtime API is a deliberately allowlisted subset of Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API and WhatsApp Business Management API. For supported operations, migrate an existing Graph request by changing:

    - https://graph.facebook.com/v25.0/...
    + https://api.dualhook.com/v25.0/...
    
    - Authorization: Bearer <META_ACCESS_TOKEN>
    + Authorization: Bearer <DH_LIVE_KEY>

Keep the supported Meta path, method, query, and JSON shape. Dualhook is not an unrestricted Graph API proxy: only the operations in the [Runtime API Endpoint Reference](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api-reference)
 are accepted. When a request fails, [Runtime API Errors](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api-errors)
 works back from the response to the fix.

Connection-Scoped Keys[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#connection-scoped-keys)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each `dh_live_...` key is bound to exactly one Dualhook connection, organization, phone-number ID, and WABA ID. It cannot be used for another connection or as a general Meta credential.

Create and Store a Key[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#create-and-store-a-key)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An organization admin creates the key from **Connection → Overview → Outbound API key**. Plaintext is displayed once. Dualhook stores only its SHA-256 hash.

Store the key in a server-side secret manager. Never put it in browser code, mobile applications, public automation exports, logs, screenshots, or support messages. Do not share, resell, sublicense, or reuse it for another customer.

    Authorization: Bearer dh_live_...

Authentication Boundary[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#authentication-boundary)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Customers submit only the `dh_live_...` credential. Never submit any of these values to the Runtime API:

*   Meta access or app access tokens
*   Meta App Secret or app ID
*   `appsecret_proof`
*   a second `Authorization` value
*   business, WABA, or phone IDs in a request body
*   Graph hosts or webhook/callback URLs

Dualhook loads the selected connection's encrypted Meta authorization inside the Worker and applies Meta App Secret Proof internally to every authenticated Graph request. Caller credentials, proof, hosts, or asset overrides are rejected rather than forwarded.

Temporary media-download URLs are the documented exception: after a proof-aware media metadata request, the Worker downloads bytes from a validated Facebook/CDN hostname using Meta's Bearer-only media-download flow. Redirects remain manual.

Rotation[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#rotation)

-----------------------------------------------------------

Rotation creates a new primary key and offers three choices for the old key:

*   revoke immediately
*   keep a one-hour grace overlap
*   keep a 24-hour grace overlap

Use an overlap only long enough to deploy the new key.

Routing Holds and Revocation[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#routing-holds-and-revocation)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A reversible billing, plan-limit, administrator, or Meta routing hold does not revoke the connection's runtime key. The key remains bound to the same connection but cannot route requests while the connection is blocked. If the final hold is released and Meta webhook routing is restored and verified, the same key works again.

Keys are invalidated by terminal connection removal, explicit key revocation or rotation, expiration of a grace key, or an administrator quarantining that credential after a security incident. Creating or rotating a key is unavailable while its connection is not routable.

connection\_not\_routable[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#connection_not_routable)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A valid key receives HTTP `403` when its connection cannot currently route requests:

    {
      "error": {
        "code": "connection_not_routable",
        "reason": "billing_unpaid",
        "message": "The subscription does not currently permit API routing.",
        "docs": "https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#connection_not_routable"
      }
    }

The `reason` is restricted to this public allowlist:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `onboarding_incomplete` | Connection setup is incomplete. |
| `plan_limit_grace` | A temporary plan-limit grace period applies. |
| `plan_limit_exceeded` | The subscription's connection limit was exceeded. |
| `billing_unpaid` | The subscription does not currently permit routing. |
| `subscription_canceled` | The subscription was canceled. |
| `admin_hold_org` | An administrator hold applies to the organization. |
| `admin_hold_connection` | An administrator hold applies to this connection. |
| `meta_banned` | Meta disabled or scheduled the account for disablement. |
| `meta_offboarded` | Meta reports that the account is offboarded. |
| `meta_messaging_restricted` | Meta restricted messaging for the connection. |
| `meta_token_invalid` | Meta authorization is invalid or expired. |
| `meta_override_inactive` | Required webhook routing is inactive. |
| `partner_removed` | Meta reports that the Dualhook connection was removed. |
| `offboarding` | Connection removal is in progress. |
| `connection_unavailable` | No more specific public reason is safely available. |

Do not rotate a key in response to this error. Resolve the connection hold in Dualhook.

Other authorization responses:

*   `401` — missing, invalid, revoked, expired, or quarantined credential.
*   `403 asset_scope_conflict` — the stored phone/WABA assets are also assigned to a conflicting active connection, so routing fails closed.
*   `403` with an object-scope message — a media or template object is owned outside the selected connection.

Request Controls[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#request-controls)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The runtime enforces exact v25.0 routes, strict content types, explicit request schemas, field/query allowlists, bounded JSON, MIME-specific media limits, asset ownership, and manual redirects.

Raw Graph pagination URLs are never accepted or returned. Use the safe `after` or `before` cursor documented in the endpoint reference; Dualhook reconstructs the Graph request internally.

Every response includes `X-Dualhook-Request-Id`. Keep it in your content-free request log for support correlation.

Rate Limits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#rate-limits)

-----------------------------------------------------------------

| Bucket | Default | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Messages | 80 operations/second | connection |
| Media upload/delete | 20 operations/minute | connection |
| Media metadata/download | 120 operations/minute | connection |
| Phone/WABA health and status | 6 operations/minute per connection; 30/minute per WABA | connection and WABA |
| Management reads | 60 weighted units/minute | connection and WABA |
| Management mutations | 10 weighted units/minute | connection and WABA |
| Failed authentication | 20 rejected attempts/minute | credential |

Phone and WABA reads share a six-per-minute connection allowance and a 30-per-minute WABA allowance. Successful responses are cached per connection for 60 seconds; `X-Dualhook-Cache` reports `hit` or `miss`, and cache hits include an `Age` header in seconds. Other single-object management reads cost 1 unit; template and QR lists cost 2. Profile, settings, and QR writes cost 2; a template header sample upload costs 4; template create/update costs 6; template deletion costs 10. One sample upload followed by one create therefore fits the default ten-unit mutation window.

After 30 failed Meta message requests within a rolling five-minute window, sending pauses for five minutes. Successful sends do not erase failures already accumulated in that window. A throttled response uses HTTP `429` and includes `Retry-After`.

Authentication is guarded separately before the database lookup. Once the database identifies a revoked or expired credential, that refusal is cached for up to 24 hours and continues returning `401`. Other rejected credentials are throttled after 20 failed attempts within a minute: further requests receive HTTP `429` with `Retry-After` for five minutes. The throttle is keyed on the credential, not on your connection or IP address, so one dead key cannot slow down your other keys, and a key that authenticates successfully never accumulates against it. If you see this, stop retrying and check that the key is still active on the connection — a key revoked by connection cleanup or by a rotation cannot be revived, and a new one must be created on the connection's Overview page.

Privacy Model[](https://dualhook.com/docs/runtime-api#privacy-model)

---------------------------------------------------------------------

Inbound customer-path webhooks remain direct from Meta to your endpoint. Outbound payloads and requested media transit Dualhook's Cloudflare Worker without body persistence or caching. Only successful, allowlisted phone/WABA metadata reads receive a connection-isolated 60-second response cache; no message, media, template, profile, or error response enters it.

Operational logs exclude request bodies, recipients, message content, media bytes, credentials, proofs, authorization headers, SIP credentials, encryption material, and raw Meta download or pagination URLs. Daily metrics contain only connection/organization scope, operation, status, latency, byte counts, safe Meta error metadata, and — on failed requests only — a truncated SHA-256 target fingerprint plus a failure reason and pipeline stage drawn from a fixed Dualhook vocabulary. The failure reason records why the runtime itself refused a request, never customer input, object IDs, or Meta message text; successful requests store no fingerprint, reason, or stage.
