# WhatsApp Embedded Signup Error Codes and Fixes | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Embedded Signup Errors
======================

Searchable Meta Embedded Signup error index with safe first actions for business, WABA, phone, OTP, sharing, and account restrictions.

This is a searchable, action-oriented index of errors Meta can show during WhatsApp Embedded Signup. Wording can vary by flow version and locale.

How to Use This Index[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#how-to-use-this-index)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Search this page for the numeric code or a distinctive phrase from Meta's dialog. Follow the first safe action before deleting or recreating any business asset. Errors displayed inside Meta's popup occur before Dualhook can inspect or change the selected asset.

Generic textual errors have these usual first steps:

| Message or situation | First safe action |
| --- | --- |
| Request failed or “Something has gone wrong” | Wait a few minutes and retry once. If it persists, capture the session ID and contact Meta Business Support. |
| Business creation limit or “one business user at a time” | Select an existing Business Portfolio or wait for Meta's creation limit to clear. |
| Facebook account too new, spam-limited, advertising-disabled, or payment-disabled | Use an established authorized admin account and resolve its restriction in Account Quality/Business Support. |
| Invalid business name | Use the real business or brand name and follow Meta's naming rules. |
| No permission to create a WABA | Obtain full admin access to the selected Business Portfolio. |
| WABA creation limited until verification | Complete [Meta Business Verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)<br> or use an eligible existing WABA. |
| Phone blocked or account cannot be verified | Review Account Quality and Business Support before retrying. |
| Phone already exists in the selected WABA | Restart the flow and choose the existing number instead of adding it again. |
| Existing WhatsApp registration | Confirm whether you are using Coexistence or migration before deregistering anything. See [Phone Numbers](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers)<br>. |
| Verified/display name rejected or under review | Wait for the current review or correct the name using [Display Names](https://dualhook.com/docs/display-names)<br>. |
| OTP guessed/requested too many times | Stop retrying and wait for the period shown by Meta; repeated attempts extend rate limits. |

What Dualhook Shows[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#what-dualhook-shows)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When Meta returns a documented numeric error to the browser, Dualhook shows a safe explanation and the first recommended action. The notice links back to this index so you can search the exact code. A Meta `CANCEL` event is shown as a cancellation and identifies the screen where the flow stopped; it is not mislabeled as a blocked popup.

For operational reconciliation and Meta support, Dualhook records only the numeric Meta error ID, Meta session ID, Meta error timestamp, and the documented `current_step` value. It does not store the raw Embedded Signup event, OAuth authorization code, Meta error text, or selected-business payload. The localized Meta message may be shown once in the browser, but is not persisted. Unknown codes remain visible by number instead of being guessed.

Do not repeatedly relaunch Embedded Signup after an eligibility, restriction, ownership, or rate-limit error. Those conditions generally require an account-side correction or a waiting period, and repeated attempts can extend Meta's limits.

Abandoned Flow Screens[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#abandoned-flow-screens)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook records the `CANCEL` screen name for attributable attempts. These values are not failures by themselves:

| Current step | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_SELECTION` | Business Portfolio selection |
| `WABA_PHONE_PROFILE_PICKER` | WABA/phone selection |
| `WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_PROFILE_SETUP` | WABA or business-profile creation |
| `PHONE_NUMBER_SETUP` | Phone-number addition |
| `PHONE_NUMBER_VERIFICATION` | OTP verification |
| `PERMISSIONS` | Permissions review |

Business Portfolio and WABA[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#business-portfolio-and-waba)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Codes | Meaning | First safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2655081`, `1752140`, `2455008` | Ad-account limit reached | Check Business Info, billing, and business verification; reuse an eligible existing ad account. |
| `2655055`, `2494149` | Ad-account link or creation failed | Retry once; escalate if the same session repeatedly fails. |
| `1752004`, `3441056`, `2446325` | Ad account/business is invalid, violates policy, or is under review | Resolve the listed issue in Business Support Home. |
| `1690214` | Payment account disabled | Ask the financial admin to resolve or appeal the disabled payment account. |
| `2388098` | More WABAs require verification | Complete business verification before creating another WABA. |
| `1752089` | Only one Business account can be created at a time | Wait or select an existing Business Portfolio. |

| `1690089`, `1690091`, `1690062`, `1690090` | Duplicate or invalid business/system-user name | Choose a distinct valid real-world name. |
| `2593010` | WABA name exceeds 255 characters | Shorten the WABA name. |
| `3771014` | Invalid link | Correct the URL. |
| `2388010`, `2388009` | Verified name cannot be edited | Read the detailed Meta reason and wait for any active name review. |

See [WhatsApp Business Accounts](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
, [Meta Business Portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
, and [Meta Business Verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)
.

Phone and Coexistence[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#phone-and-coexistence)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Codes | Meaning | First safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `2655095`, `2655048` | Number is not registered with WhatsApp Business | Register it in WhatsApp Business or use an already registered Business number. |

| `3441030` | Number is already registered elsewhere | Decide whether this should be Coexistence or migration before deregistering. |
| `3441047` | Account using Marketing Messages is not eligible for this flow | Select another eligible WABA or resolve the incompatible product enrollment. |

Verification and Rate Limits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#verification-and-rate-limits)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| `2593039`, `2388093` | Verification code could not be verified | Re-enter the current code once; if it fails, wait for Meta's retry window. |
| `2494158` | Too many OTP requests | Stop requesting codes and wait for the limit to clear. |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| `2593035` | Phone creation failed | Recheck the number; escalate if the same valid number keeps failing. |
| `1357053` | Account restricted from this action | Review Account Quality and resolve the restriction. |

| `1752206` | User cannot be added to the business | Verify the user's admin access or contact Meta. |

 before retrying restricted accounts.

Authentication and Pages[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#authentication-and-pages)

Still Stuck[](https://dualhook.com/docs/embedded-signup-errors#still-stuck)

# WhatsApp Service Messages: CSW, Types, TTL, and Pricing | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Service Messages
================

Free-form messages inside an open customer service window: types, replies, TTL, and October 2026 pricing with 1,000 free messages per number each month.

What Service Messages Are[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#what-service-messages-are)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Service messages are **free-form** messages sent through the Cloud API `/messages` endpoint. They are the counterpart to template messages: where templates are pre-approved formats sent in any window, service messages are composed on the fly and only sendable inside an open customer service window (CSW).

|     | Service messages | Template messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-approval required? | No  | Yes |
| When can you send? | Inside an open 24-hour CSW only | Any time, with a paid send if outside CSW |
| Composition | Free-form | Bound to approved template structure |
| Categories | Service (or `free_customer_service` for utility templates inside CSW) | `MARKETING` / `UTILITY` / `AUTHENTICATION` |
| Pricing object `category` | `service` | `marketing`, `utility`, `authentication`, etc. |

Use service messages to respond conversationally inside an active customer interaction. To message a user outside any CSW, you must use [marketing](https://dualhook.com/docs/marketing-messages)
, [utility](https://dualhook.com/docs/utility-messages)
, or [authentication](https://dualhook.com/docs/authentication-messages)
 templates.

Service Pages in This Section[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#service-pages-in-this-section)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   [Interactive Service Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-interactive)
     — CTA URL button, list, media carousel, reply buttons, location request
*   [Address Messages (India)](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address)
     — interactive form to collect a shipping address from Indian recipients
*   [Reaction Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-reactions)
     — emoji reactions on a previous user message
*   [Media Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages)
     — image, video, audio, document, sticker
*   [Contacts & Location Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-location)
     — share contact cards or location coordinates

The Customer Service Window[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#the-customer-service-window)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When a WhatsApp user messages or calls you, a **24-hour timer** (the customer service window or CSW) starts. While that window is open, you can send any service message type listed below. Each new inbound message or call from the user resets the timer to 24 hours.

When the window closes, you can only send pre-approved [template messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
.

You may only send messages to WhatsApp users who have opted in to receiving messages from you — the open window is a permission to respond, not a license to broadcast.

In rare cases, an inbound message from a user may not open the CSW for you to respond. This is a known platform-level edge case.

Message Types[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#message-types)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

The service-message types you can send during an open CSW:

| Type | What it is | Where documented |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | Text body with optional link preview | [Messaging Overview](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-overview) |
| `image` | Single image with optional caption | [Media Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages) |
| `video` | Video with optional caption | [Media Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages) |
| `audio` | Voice message or basic audio | [Media Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages) |
| `document` | File with download icon | [Media Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages) |
| `sticker` | Static or animated WebP sticker | [Media Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages) |
| `location` | Location coordinates | [Contacts & Location](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-location) |
| `contacts` | Contact card with up to 257 contacts | [Contacts & Location](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-location) |
| `reaction` | Emoji reaction on a previous user message | [Reactions](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-reactions) |
| `interactive` (`cta_url`) | URL mapped to a button | [Interactive Service Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-interactive) |
| `interactive` (`list`) | List of options in a modal | [Interactive Service Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-interactive) |
| `interactive` (`button`) | Up to 3 reply buttons | [Interactive Service Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-interactive) |
| `interactive` (`carousel`) | Horizontally scrollable media cards | [Interactive Service Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-interactive) |
| `interactive` (`location_request_message`) | Send-location button | [Interactive Service Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-interactive) |
| `interactive` (`address_message`) | Address-collection form (India only) | [Address Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address) |
| `interactive` (`flow`) | Structured Flow message | Meta WhatsApp Flows docs |

Core Endpoint[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#core-endpoint)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

All service messages use the same endpoint:

    POST https://api.dualhook.com/v25.0/<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/messages

The body shape is consistent across types — the `type` field selects the message kind and the matching property carries the contents:

    {
      "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
      "recipient_type": "individual",
      "to": "12015550123",
      "type": "<MESSAGE_TYPE>",
      "<MESSAGE_TYPE>": { /* contents */ }
    }

`recipient_type` is `individual` for 1-to-1 messages or `group` for group messaging (see Meta's Groups API docs).

A successful response returns the WhatsApp message ID immediately, but **does not confirm delivery** — delivery status arrives asynchronously via a [status webhook](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-webhook)
. For full status-lifecycle behavior, see [Messaging Overview](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-overview#delivery-status-lifecycle)
.

WhatsApp User Phone Number Formats[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#whatsapp-user-phone-number-formats)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Plus signs (`+`), hyphens, parentheses, and spaces are all permitted in the `to` field. Strongly include both the `+` and country calling code — without them, your business phone number's own country code may be prepended, sending the message to the wrong recipient.

| Sent | Delivered to | Outcome (business in India, country code 91) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+16315551234` | `+16315551234` | Correct |
| `+1 (631) 555-1234` | `+16315551234` | Correct |
| `(631) 555-1234` | `+916315551234` | Wrong number — country code prepended |
| `1 (631) 555-1234` | `+9116315551234` | Wrong number — country code prepended |

For Brazil and Mexico, Cloud API may modify the prefix automatically — this is by design, not a bug.

Contextual Replies[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#contextual-replies)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

You can send a service message as a contextual reply to a specific previous message. WhatsApp displays it with a quote bubble pointing to the message you're replying to. Pass the original message's `wamid` in the `context` object on your send call:

    {
      "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
      "to": "12015550123",
      "context": { "message_id": "wamid.HBgLM..." },
      "type": "text",
      "text": { "body": "Yes, that order ships tomorrow." }
    }

This makes it easier for the user to know which specific message you are replying to — useful in long, multi-thread conversations.

Media Caching (Hosted URLs)[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#media-caching-hosted-urls)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When you send media via the `link` property (a URL on your public server) instead of `id` (an uploaded media asset), Cloud API fetches the asset and **caches it for 10 minutes**. Subsequent sends with the **same** URL within that window reuse the cached copy.

To bypass the cache (e.g. you re-uploaded under the same path), append a random query string:

    First send:  https://link.to.media/sample.jpg          → fetched, cached 10 min
    Second send: https://link.to.media/sample.jpg          → cached copy reused
    Third send:  https://link.to.media/sample.jpg?abc123   → fetched, cached 10 min
    

This is also why Meta recommends `id` over `link` for production sends — uploaded media has a stable identifier and avoids the caching footgun entirely. See [Media Messages → Send Media by Media ID](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages#send-media-by-media-id)
.

Delivery Sequence of Multiple Messages[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#delivery-sequence-of-multiple-messages)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When sending a series of messages, **delivery order is not guaranteed to match request order**. If sequence matters (e.g. an intro message before a follow-up question), wait for the `delivered` status webhook on message N before sending message N+1.

For high-volume bursts where strict ordering doesn't matter (e.g. a list of independent updates), pipeline freely.

Time-To-Live (TTL) and Dropped Messages[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#time-to-live-ttl-and-dropped-messages)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If Cloud API can't deliver a message immediately (recipient offline, network issue), it retries for a default TTL window:

| Message kind | Default TTL |
| --- | --- |
| All service messages | 30 days |
| Authentication templates | 10 minutes |
| All other templates | 30 days |

You can customize TTL per template (utility, authentication, and marketing-via-MM-API only). See Meta's Time-to-live documentation for the full TTL parameter reference.

If you don't receive a `delivered` status webhook before the TTL elapses, **assume the message was dropped**. Failed sends emit a `failed` status webhook, but with a small possible delay — build a buffer before treating absence as failure.

Message Quality[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#message-quality)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quality is computed from the last seven days of recipient feedback signals, weighted by recency: blocks, reports, mutes, archives, and the reasons users provide when blocking you.

To keep quality high:

*   Follow the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy.
*   Only message users who have explicitly opted in.
*   Make messages personalized and useful — avoid generic greetings.
*   Don't send too many messages per day.
*   Optimize content and length for the audience.

Per-number status, quality rating, and messaging limits are visible in WhatsApp Manager → Account tools → Phone numbers, and are also surfaced via [Health Monitoring](https://dualhook.com/docs/health-monitoring)
 in Dualhook. High-traffic numbers can shift quality state within minutes — see [Capacity, Quality & Limits](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits)
 for monitoring guidance.

Pricing[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages#pricing)

--------------------------------------------------------------

Through **September 30, 2026**, service messages sent inside an open CSW are free. From **October 1, 2026**, each phone number gets 1,000 free service messages per month; only the 1,001st onward is charged. The allowance refreshes monthly, does not roll over, and is separate for each phone number. Paid service messages use the utility and authentication list rate for the recipient's market and do not receive volume-tier discounts.

Service messages inside a 72-hour free entry point window remain free. The status-webhook `pricing.category` remains `service`; read `billable` and `type` to determine how Meta treated a delivery. Meta has documented `type: regular` for a billable service message but has not yet documented the exact `type` for a delivery covered by the new monthly free tier. See [Pricing → Free vs Billed Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/pricing#free-vs-billed-messages)
 and [WhatsApp Pricing Changes 2026](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-pricing-changes-2026)
.

# Address Messages (India) | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Address Messages (India)
========================

India-only interactive form for collecting structured shipping addresses inside WhatsApp. Covers prefill, saved addresses, validation errors, the nfm\_reply submission webhook, and feature-not-supported (error 1026) fallback.

What Address Messages Do[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#what-address-messages-do)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Address messages are an interactive [service message](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages)
 type that asks a WhatsApp user to fill in a structured shipping address inside WhatsApp itself. The user sees a form, completes it, and submits — your backend receives the structured address back via webhook.

This eliminates the back-and-forth of asking for street, pin code, city, etc. as separate text questions and avoids typos in free-form text.

Availability (India Only)[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#availability-india-only)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This feature is **only available for businesses based in India sending to Indian customers**. The form only shows on WhatsApp clients that support `address_message`. Older or non-supporting clients receive nothing visible — see [Feature Not Supported](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#feature-not-supported-old-clients)
 for the webhook you get instead.

`country` is a mandatory field in the action parameters; omitting it returns a validation error. Currently only `IN` is supported.

Supported Fields[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#supported-fields)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Field | Display label | Input type | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Name | text | —   |
| `phone_number` | Phone Number | tel | Valid phone numbers only |
| `in_pin_code` | Pin Code | text | Max length: 6 |
| `house_number` | Flat/House Number | text | —   |
| `floor_number` | Floor Number | text | —   |
| `tower_number` | Tower Number | text | —   |
| `building_name` | Building/Apartment Name | text | —   |
| `address` | Address | text | —   |
| `landmark_area` | Landmark/Area | text | —   |
| `city` | City | text | —   |
| `state` | State | text | —   |

Send an Address Message[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#send-an-address-message)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Minimal payload — just the country and a body prompt:

    {
      "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
      "recipient_type": "individual",
      "to": "+91xxxxxxxxxx",
      "type": "interactive",
      "interactive": {
        "type": "address_message",
        "body": {
          "text": "Thanks for your order! Tell us what address you'd like this delivered to."
        },
        "action": {
          "name": "address_message",
          "parameters": { "country": "IN" }
        }
      }
    }

The user sees an empty form, fills it in, submits — and you receive the address via [webhook](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#address-submission-webhook)
.

Prefill and Saved Addresses[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#prefill-and-saved-addresses)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Two optional ways to reduce the user's friction:

**Prefill specific fields** with `values`:

    "action": {
      "name": "address_message",
      "parameters": {
        "country": "IN",
        "values": {
          "name": "Pablo Morales",
          "phone_number": "+91xxxxxxxxxx"
        }
      }
    }

The user can edit prefilled values before submitting.

**Pass saved addresses** the user can pick from:

    "action": {
      "name": "address_message",
      "parameters": {
        "country": "IN",
        "saved_addresses": [\
          {\
            "id": "address1",\
            "value": {\
              "name": "Pablo Morales",\
              "phone_number": "+91xxxxxxxxxx",\
              "in_pin_code": "400063",\
              "floor_number": "8",\
              "building_name": "",\
              "address": "Wing A, Cello Triumph, IB Patel Rd",\
              "landmark_area": "Goregaon",\
              "city": "Mumbai"\
            }\
          }\
        ]
      }
    }

The user sees the saved addresses with an option to pick one or enter a new address. Each saved address needs a unique `id` you assign — when the user picks one, the webhook returns that `id` so you can map it back to your CRM record.

Validation Errors[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#validation-errors)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When you receive a submitted address that fails server-side validation, **re-send** the address message with the same `values` and a `validation_errors` map. WhatsApp blocks submission until the user fixes the flagged fields.

    "action": {
      "name": "address_message",
      "parameters": {
        "country": "IN",
        "values": {
          "name": "Pablo Morales",
          "phone_number": "+91xxxxxxxxxx",
          "in_pin_code": "666666",
          "address": "Some other location",
          "city": "Delhi"
        },
        "validation_errors": {
          "in_pin_code": "We could not locate this pin code."
        }
      }
    }

`validation_errors` is a flat map of `field_name → error_message`. The error text is shown to the user beneath the offending field.

Address Submission Webhook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#address-submission-webhook)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When the user submits, you receive a Native Flow Message (NFM) reply on the standard `messages` webhook field:

    {
      "messages": [\
        {\
          "context": {\
            "from": "15550001234",\
            "id": "wamid.HBgLMTIwNjU1NTAxMDcVAgARGBI3NjNFN0U5QzMzNDlCQjY0M0QA"\
          },\
          "from": "+91xxxxxxxxxx",\
          "id": "wamid.HBgLMTIwNjU1NTAxMDcVAgASGCA5RDhBNENEMEQ3RENEOEEzMEI0RUExRDczN0I1NThFQwA=",\
          "timestamp": "1671498855",\
          "type": "interactive",\
          "interactive": {\
            "type": "nfm_reply",\
            "nfm_reply": {\
              "name": "address_message",\
              "response_json": "{\"saved_address_id\":\"address1\",\"values\":{\"in_pin_code\":\"400063\",\"building_name\":\"\",\"landmark_area\":\"Goregaon\",\"address\":\"Wing A, Cello Triumph, IB Patel Rd\",\"city\":\"Mumbai\",\"name\":\"Pablo Morales\",\"phone_number\":\"+91xxxxxxxxxx\",\"floor_number\":\"8\"}}",\
              "body": "Pablo Morales\n +91xxxxxxxxxx\n 400063, Goregaon, Wing A, Cello Triumph, IB Patel Rd, Mumbai, 8"\
            }\
          }\
        }\
      ]
    }

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `interactive.type` | Always `nfm_reply` |
| `nfm_reply.name` | Always `address_message` for this flow |
| `nfm_reply.response_json` | **String-encoded JSON** containing `saved_address_id` (if user picked a saved one) and `values` (the submitted form fields) |
| `nfm_reply.body` | Human-readable summary as the user sees it (optional) |

`response_json` is a string, not a nested object — parse it with `JSON.parse` before consuming. In Dualhook setups, this webhook arrives on the `messages` field and is delivered directly to your endpoint via [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
.

Feature Not Supported (Old Clients)[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#feature-not-supported-old-clients)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If the recipient's WhatsApp client doesn't support `address_message` (older versions, certain platforms), the message is silently dropped and you receive a `failed` status webhook with error code **1026** (Receiver Incapable):

    {
      "statuses": [\
        {\
          "id": "wamid.HBgL...",\
          "status": "failed",\
          "timestamp": "1670394125",\
          "type": "message",\
          "recipient_id": "91xxxxxxxxxx",\
          "errors": [\
            { "code": 1026, "title": "Receiver Incapable" }\
          ]\
        }\
      ]
    }

Treat 1026 as "fall back to a text-based address question" — the user did not refuse, they just can't see the form.

Typical Flow[](https://dualhook.com/docs/service-messages-address#typical-flow)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Business sends an `address_message` (with `parameters.country: "IN"`, optionally `values` or `saved_addresses`).
2.  User taps the CTA, fills the form, submits.
3.  Webhook arrives with `type: "interactive"`, `interactive.type: "nfm_reply"`, `nfm_reply.name: "address_message"`, `nfm_reply.response_json` containing the address.
4.  Backend validates server-side (e.g. real pin-code lookup, courier coverage check).
5.  If validation fails, re-send the message with `values` (carrying over the user's input) plus `validation_errors`.
6.  Loop until validation passes or user abandons.

If the recipient's client doesn't support the form, the send fails with error 1026 and you should fall back to text-based collection.

# Capacity, Quality & Limits | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Capacity, Quality & Limits
==========================

API rate limits, messaging limit tiers, quality rating, and scaling guidance.

Throughput[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#throughput)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each business [phone number](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers)
 can send up to **80 messages per second** by default (combined inbound and outbound across text, media, and template messages). Higher capacity is available through Meta on request.

Throughput is per phone number, not per portfolio — adding more numbers under the same WABA is one way to scale total send rate.

API Rate Limits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#api-rate-limits)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Two layers of rate limiting apply at the Graph API level:

### App-level call limits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#app-level-call-limits)

Calls your app makes against a WABA count toward an app-level request budget over a rolling one-hour window:

| WABA state | Default limit (per app, per WABA) |
| --- | --- |
| New WABA, no registered phone number | 200 requests / hour |
| Active WABA with at least one registered phone number | 5,000 requests / hour |

These limits apply to management endpoints such as `/<WABA_ID>`, `/<WABA_ID>/phone_numbers`, `/<WABA_ID>/message_templates`, `/<WABA_ID>/subscribed_apps`, and `/<WABA_ID>/assigned_users`.

### Runtime symptoms[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#runtime-symptoms)

Rate limiting can also occur even when your account is healthy. Two common runtime modes:

*   **Request-rate limit** — returns `429` when request-per-second thresholds are exceeded.
*   **Concurrent-load limit** — returns `503` when upstream systems are temporarily overloaded.

If either appears:

1.  Slow down request pace immediately.
2.  Use queue-based traffic shaping.
3.  Retry with exponential backoff and jitter.

For error code details, see [Meta API Error Reference](https://dualhook.com/docs/api-errors)
.

Pair Rate Limit (Per Recipient)[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#pair-rate-limit-per-recipient)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Independent of throughput, a single business phone number can only send **1 message every 6 seconds to the same WhatsApp user** (≈10 messages/minute, 600/hour per pair). Exceeding this returns error `131056` until the pair is back within the allowed rate.

Bursting is allowed: up to **45 messages in a 6-second burst** to the same user, but each burst "borrows" from future quota — after a burst of 20, you must wait roughly 2 minutes before sending more to that recipient.

Recommended retry on `131056`: back off `4^X` seconds (start with `X=0`, increment on each repeated failure) until the send succeeds. The full symptom, cause, and fix guide is on [WhatsApp Error 131056](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-error-131056)
.

Messaging Limits (Portfolio-Level)[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#messaging-limits-portfolio-level)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Messaging limits define how many unique users your business can message outside the customer service window in a rolling 24-hour period.

Limits are shared at the [Meta Business Portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
 level — all numbers in the same portfolio consume the same messaging pool.

Typical tiers:

| Tier | Unique users / 24h |
| --- | --- |
| `TIER_250` | 250 |
| `TIER_2K` | 2,000 |
| `TIER_10K` | 10,000 |
| `TIER_100K` | 100,000 |
| `TIER_UNLIMITED` | No cap |

**Important:** User-initiated conversations are not counted toward this limit. Limits only apply to business-initiated outreach outside the service window.

Limit Fields[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#limit-fields)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta shifted to portfolio-level limit handling on **October 7, 2025**. Request the current portfolio-level field when checking status from the phone-number node.

| Field | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `whatsapp_business_manager_messaging_limit` | Current (portfolio-level) |
| `current_limit` | Used in some webhook events |

Dualhook uses `whatsapp_business_manager_messaging_limit` for new health checks. Some management webhook events still include `current_limit`, so keep handling that event payload field separately.

Increasing Limits[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#increasing-limits)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Limit growth happens in stages:

1.  Scale from `250` to `2,000`
2.  Scale from `2,000` upward (`10K`, `100K`, unlimited)

Common qualification factors:

*   [Business verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-verification)
     path completion
*   Consistent high-quality messaging
*   Sufficient recent usage of current limit

After eligibility is met, upgrades are often applied automatically within a few hours.

### Automatic Scaling Beyond 2,000[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#automatic-scaling-beyond-2000)

Meta evaluates:

*   Message quality across numbers and [templates](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
    
*   Utilization of current limit over the last 7 days

If criteria are satisfied, the portfolio moves up one tier automatically.

Quality Rating[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#quality-rating)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quality is based on recent user feedback signals, weighted by recency:

*   Blocks
*   Reports
*   Read/engagement behavior
*   Negative feedback patterns

When quality degrades:

*   Upgrade eligibility can be delayed
*   Sending restrictions can appear
*   Health may move from `AVAILABLE` to `LIMITED` or `BLOCKED` (see [Health Monitoring](https://dualhook.com/docs/health-monitoring)
    )

Template Quality States[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#template-quality-states)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[Template](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
\-level quality is tracked separately from number-level health.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ACTIVE - QUALITY_PENDING` | Not enough data to rate |
| `ACTIVE - HIGH QUALITY` | Strong user satisfaction |
| `ACTIVE - MEDIUM QUALITY` | Early dissatisfaction signals |
| `ACTIVE - LOW QUALITY` | High dissatisfaction risk |

Low template quality can lead to pauses or disablement even if account-level access is still active.

Check Current Status[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#check-current-status)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

React to `phone_number_quality_update`, `account_update`, `account_review_update`, and `business_capability_update` webhooks first. Use the read below only for reconciliation, at most once every five minutes. The phone health response includes the related WABA, business, and app summary, so do not poll the WABA separately for the same health check.

    curl -X GET "https://api.dualhook.com/v25.0/<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>?fields=health_status,quality_rating,whatsapp_business_manager_messaging_limit" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer <DH_LIVE_KEY>"

    {
      "id": "<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>",
      "health_status": {
        "can_send_message": "AVAILABLE",
        "entities": []
      },
      "quality_rating": "GREEN",
      "whatsapp_business_manager_messaging_limit": "TIER_10K"
    }

Webhook Signals to Monitor[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#webhook-signals-to-monitor)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook surfaces management events for operations monitoring. See [Webhook Events](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-events)
 for the complete event list.

### phone\_number\_quality\_update[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#phone_number_quality_update)

    {
      "object": "whatsapp_business_account",
      "entry": [\
        {\
          "id": "<WABA_ID>",\
          "changes": [\
            {\
              "field": "phone_number_quality_update",\
              "value": {\
                "event": "QUALITY_UPDATED",\
                "phone_number_id": "<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>",\
                "display_phone_number": "<BUSINESS_DISPLAY_PHONE_NUMBER>",\
                "current_limit": "TIER_2K",\
                "current_quality_rating": "YELLOW",\
                "previous_quality_rating": "GREEN"\
              }\
            }\
          ]\
        }\
      ]
    }

### business\_capability\_update[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#business_capability_update)

    {
      "object": "whatsapp_business_account",
      "entry": [\
        {\
          "id": "<WABA_ID>",\
          "changes": [\
            {\
              "field": "business_capability_update",\
              "value": {\
                "event": "increased_capabilities_eligibility_deferred"\
              }\
            }\
          ]\
        }\
      ]
    }

Monitoring Locations[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#monitoring-locations)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use both product and Meta surfaces:

*   **Dualhook dashboard** — webhook-driven health and limit/quality signals
*   **WhatsApp Manager** — Messaging Limits and account insights
*   **Meta Account Quality** — `business.facebook.com/accountquality`

Operational Playbook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits#operational-playbook)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If quality drops or limit upgrades stall:

1.  Reduce promotional volume and tighten audience targeting.
2.  Send only to recently opted-in users.
3.  Improve [template](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
     relevance and frequency control.
4.  Monitor blocks/reports daily and pause weak campaigns quickly.
5.  Resume scale gradually only after sustained quality recovery.

For a comprehensive health maintenance strategy, see [Maintain Account Health](https://dualhook.com/docs/account-health)
.

# Dualhook + Zapier: Gateway Pattern for WhatsApp Webhooks and Template Sends | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Zapier Webhook Integration
==========================

Use a lightweight gateway for Meta verification, then forward approved WhatsApp events into Zapier for downstream automation.

Prerequisites[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#prerequisites)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   An active [Dualhook connection](https://dualhook.com/docs/getting-started)
    
*   A lightweight HTTPS gateway endpoint that you control
*   Your Meta webhook verify token (for the GET handshake — set during connection setup in Dualhook)
*   Your `WABA_ID` and `PHONE_NUMBER_ID` for payload-side validation in the gateway
*   A Zapier account with either:
    *   **Webhooks by Zapier** for receiving forwarded events, or
    *   **API by Zapier** / **Webhooks by Zapier** for outbound Graph API requests

If you need a starting point for the gateway itself, use one of the direct receiver guides:

*   [Node.js Webhook Receiver](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-nodejs-webhook)
    
*   [Laravel Webhook Integration](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-laravel-webhook)
    

Why Zapier Is Not the Direct Meta Webhook Receiver[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#why-zapier-is-not-the-direct-meta-webhook-receiver)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook's direct-routing model expects your Meta callback URL to complete Meta's verification handshake:

*   Meta sends `GET` with `hub.mode`, `hub.verify_token`, and `hub.challenge`
*   your endpoint must return the raw `hub.challenge` body with `200`

Zapier's Catch Hook and Catch Raw Hook triggers can receive webhook traffic, but they do not provide the response control needed to reliably act as the Meta verification endpoint. That makes Zapier a poor fit for the first hop in a Dualhook webhook flow.

Zapier is still useful after the first hop. The safe pattern is:

1.  a small gateway endpoint receives Meta webhooks
2.  the gateway validates the payload and responds to Meta
3.  the gateway forwards approved events into Zapier

> **No `META_APP_SECRET`?** In the Embedded Signup flow `X-Hub-Signature-256` is signed by Dualhook's Meta app and isn't customer-verifiable — the gateway validates inbound webhook payload shape instead. See [Messaging Webhook → Inbound Webhook POST Validation](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-webhook#signature-validation-post)
> .

Architecture Overview[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#architecture-overview)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Meta (messages, statuses, errors)
      -> Your gateway endpoint
         -> GET verification (verify_token)
         -> inbound payload validation (envelope, WABA ID, phone_number_id)
         -> fast 200 to Meta
         -> forward normalized event to Zapier
    
    Zapier
      -> downstream automation
      -> optional sends through api.dualhook.com
    
    Dualhook
      -> setup, monitoring, template operations, management events

This keeps Dualhook out of message storage while still acknowledging that your gateway and Zapier can both become storage layers if they keep request bodies, task history, or logs.

Build the Gateway Endpoint[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#build-the-gateway-endpoint)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The gateway can be a small Node.js service, Laravel controller, edge function, or similar HTTPS endpoint. It must do four things reliably.

### 1\. Handle GET verification[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#1-handle-get-verification)

For `GET` verification requests:

*   verify that `hub.mode` is `subscribe`
*   compare `hub.verify_token` to your expected token
*   return the raw `hub.challenge` value with `200`
*   return `403` on mismatch

### 2\. Validate inbound POST payloads[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#2-validate-inbound-post-payloads)

For `POST` webhook requests:

*   confirm `object === "whatsapp_business_account"`
*   confirm `entry[].id` equals your stored `WABA_ID`
*   confirm `entry[].changes[].field` is `messages`
*   confirm `value.metadata.phone_number_id` is present and equals your stored `PHONE_NUMBER_ID`
*   return `401` and stop if any check fails

### 3\. Respond quickly[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#3-respond-quickly)

Return `200` to Meta immediately after inbound payload validation passes. Do heavy work asynchronously.

### 4\. Forward a normalized event into Zapier[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#4-forward-a-normalized-event-into-zapier)

Forward only what Zapier needs. A practical forwarded shape includes:

    {
      "trace_id": "internal_trace_id",
      "received_at": "2026-04-08T12:00:00Z",
      "event_type": "messages",
      "phone_number_id": "123456789012345",
      "payload": {
        "object": "whatsapp_business_account",
        "entry": []
      }
    }

If you want the gateway reference implementation, adapt the verification and payload-validation logic from [Node.js Webhook Receiver](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-nodejs-webhook)
 or [Laravel Webhook Integration](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-laravel-webhook)
.

Trigger Zapier from the Gateway[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#trigger-zapier-from-the-gateway)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If the gateway is forwarding normalized JSON, **Catch Hook** is usually the simplest Zap trigger. Use **Catch Raw Hook** only when you deliberately want the forwarded body unparsed and are sure it stays within Zapier's size limits.

Recommended pattern:

1.  Build a Zap with **Webhooks by Zapier** as the trigger.
2.  Copy the Zapier hook URL.
3.  Have the gateway `POST` the normalized event to that URL after Meta has already received `200`.
4.  Continue the rest of your automation in Zapier.

This split keeps the Meta-facing contract under your control and keeps Zapier focused on downstream automation, notifications, enrichment, or app-to-app steps.

Send Template Messages via Dualhook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#send-template-messages-via-dualhook)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For outbound sends from Zapier, prefer **API by Zapier** when you want credentials stored in an app connection rather than inside a Zap step. Use **Webhooks by Zapier** only when simple auth or no auth is enough and you accept step-level credential visibility.

### Preferred: API by Zapier[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#preferred-api-by-zapier)

Use **API by Zapier -> API Request** with:

*   Method: `POST`
*   URL: `https://api.dualhook.com/v25.0/<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/messages`
*   Authentication: static headers or OAuth if your setup requires it
*   Domain filter: restrict to `api.dualhook.com`

### Simpler fallback: Webhooks by Zapier[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#simpler-fallback-webhooks-by-zapier)

If you are comfortable with step-level auth handling, **Webhooks by Zapier** can also send the request:

*   Method: `POST`
*   Headers:
    *   `Authorization: Bearer <DUALHOOK_API_KEY>`
    *   `Content-Type: application/json`

Example template send:

    {
      "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
      "to": "12015550123",
      "type": "template",
      "template": {
        "name": "order_update_v1",
        "language": { "code": "en_US" }
      }
    }

See [Sending Template Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/sending-template-messages)
 for richer payload patterns.

Test with Dualhook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#test-with-dualhook)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Put the gateway URL, not the Zapier URL, into Dualhook as the webhook URL.
2.  Use the same verify token in Dualhook and in the gateway.
3.  Confirm the gateway completes Meta verification successfully.
4.  Run Dualhook **Test Ping** to confirm the endpoint is reachable.
5.  Send a real WhatsApp message to your number.
6.  Confirm that:
    *   the gateway accepts real Meta payloads and rejects unrelated test pings
    *   Meta receives a fast `200`
    *   the gateway forwards the event to Zapier
    *   the Zap runs on the forwarded event

Production Caveats[](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-zapier-webhook#production-caveats)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Do not use Zapier as the primary durability layer for Meta webhooks. The gateway should own retries, idempotency, and backoff when Zapier is slow or rate-limited.
*   Zapier can delay processing under high load, and webhook/task histories can retain payload data. Treat that as part of your compliance boundary.
*   Catch Raw Hook payloads are capped at 2 MB. Keep forwarded events small and predictable.
*   Use idempotency in the gateway before forwarding and in Zapier before acting on repeated events.
*   Treat message payloads as evolving. The BSUID rollout makes some identifiers conditional, so your gateway normalization should not assume phone-number-based fields are always present. See [BSUID Transition Guide](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-bsuid)
    .

-------

*   [Node.js Webhook Receiver](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-nodejs-webhook)
    Set up a Node.js Express endpoint to receive WhatsApp webhooks routed by Dualhook.
*   [Laravel Webhook Integration](https://dualhook.com/docs/guide-laravel-webhook)
    Build a Laravel webhook controller for WhatsApp messages routed through Dualhook.

# WhatsApp Messaging Best Practices: Opt-In, Quality, Webhooks, Launch Checklist | Dualhook

Browse Docs

Messaging Best Practices
========================

Opt-in, notification quality, contact validation, callback handling, and pre-launch checklist.

The practices that keep a WhatsApp number's quality rating green and its messaging limits growing: explicit opt-in per category, notification quality rules, E.164 contact validation, idempotent sends, and a webhook receiver that acknowledges fast. Because Dualhook routes message-path webhooks straight to your server, most of this applies to code you own, and the pre-launch checklist at the end is the one Dualhook support asks about first.

Scope in Dualhook[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#scope-in-dualhook)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Because Dualhook uses [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
, message webhooks (`messages`, `statuses`, `errors`) go directly from Meta to your endpoint. These best practices primarily apply to your sending service and your webhook receiver.

Opt-In and Consent[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#opt-in-and-consent)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Active user consent is required before business-initiated messaging.

*   Collect opt-in through explicit user action.
*   Separate opt-ins by message category when possible (`marketing`, `utility`, `authentication`).
*   Make opt-out instructions clear and easy to use.
*   Store consent evidence (source, timestamp, channel, category) for auditability.

**Policy reminder:** Business-initiated outreach must use approved [templates](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
. Sending without consent increases blocks and reports, which reduces [quality and sending limits](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits)
.

Notification Quality Rules[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#notification-quality-rules)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For notification traffic, messages should be:

*   **Expected** — the recipient understands why they received it.
*   **Relevant** — content is concise, useful, and contextual.
*   **Timely** — sent when it is most useful.

Poor quality signals (blocks/reports) can lead to reduced messaging limits, temporary restrictions, and account suspension risk.

Contact Validation[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#contact-validation)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Validate phone numbers in E.164 format before sending.

Important behavior:

*   `POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/contacts` can validate whether a phone number is registered on WhatsApp and return `wa_id`, but it does not return the new BSUID `user_id` values.
*   `wa_id` is returned on successful phone-number sends. With Meta's BSUID rollout and later username launch, `wa_id` may be omitted from webhooks if the user has adopted a WhatsApp username and none of the [phone-number inclusion conditions](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-bsuid#when-phone-numbers-still-appear)
     are met. The new `user_id` (BSUID) field is the stable identifier going forward.
*   Handle `131026` (`Message Undeliverable`) as a likely invalid or unreachable recipient case.

See the [BSUID transition guide](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-bsuid)
 for the full timeline, and the [BSUID webhook changes reference](https://dualhook.com/docs/contacts-bsuid-webhooks)
 for field-level migration guidance.

### Successful Send Response[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#successful-send-response)

    {
      "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
      "contacts": [\
        {\
          "input": "12015550123",\
          "wa_id": "12015550123"\
        }\
      ],
      "messages": [\
        {\
          "id": "wamid.HBgLMTIwMTU1NTAxMjMVAgARGBI..."\
        }\
      ]
    }

Message Sending Reliability[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#message-sending-reliability)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

General rules:

*   Use `POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/messages` for all message types.
*   Stop free-form replies if you receive `470` (expired customer service window) and switch to templates.
*   Keep text message bodies at `<= 4096` characters.
*   If `preview_url: true`, ensure a valid URL is present in the message body.

Media rules:

*   Respect supported MIME types, codecs, and file-size limits (see [Media Messages](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-messages)
    ).
*   For repeated sends, upload once and reuse `media_id` instead of repeatedly passing hosted URLs (see [Upload, Retrieve & Delete Media](https://dualhook.com/docs/media-upload)
    ).

### Deep Links[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#deep-links)

Prefer Universal Links over app deep links for broader cross-device reliability:

    https://wa.me/<YOUR_WABA_PHONE_NUMBER>?text=<YOUR_URL_ENCODED_START_MESSAGE>

Callback Handling[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#callback-handling)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Design your webhook receiver as: **acknowledge first, process later.**

*   Return `HTTP 200` immediately after authenticity and basic validation.
*   Queue and process business logic asynchronously.
*   Deduplicate webhook events using `wamid` + status fields.
*   Keep certificate chain valid and DNS publicly resolvable for your callback host.

See [Messaging Webhook](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-webhook)
 for payload structure and implementation details.

Latency and Delivery Expectations[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#latency-and-delivery-expectations)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Not all delays are API-side. Delivery delays can be caused by recipient device or network conditions (low connectivity, app backgrounding, OS notification delays).

When troubleshooting:

1.  Verify webhook ack latency and error rate first.
2.  Confirm message status webhooks are arriving (`sent`, `delivered`, `read`).
3.  Confirm recipient device, app, and network state if delivery appears delayed.

Chatbot Integrations[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#chatbot-integrations)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

During rollout, set a clear fallback message when bot capability is incomplete:

    Thanks for contacting us. This automation is currently in rollout and may not answer all requests yet. For urgent help, reply HUMAN.

### Chatbot Quality Checklist[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#chatbot-quality-checklist)

Before launch, review:

*   **Branding** — tone and language match your brand.
*   **Performance** — bot intent is clear and answers common queries correctly.
*   **Consistency** — flows are reliable and regularly updated.
*   **Humanity** — bot identifies itself and exposes clear human handoff options.

**Policy requirement:** If automation cannot resolve an issue, provide a human escalation path (live agent handoff, support phone, support email/web form, or equivalent).

Pre-Launch Checklist[](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-best-practices#pre-launch-checklist)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Before scaling sends:

1.  Verify category-specific opt-ins are in place.
2.  Confirm [template](https://dualhook.com/docs/templates)
     quality and status is healthy.
3.  Warm up new numbers gradually.
4.  Test with internal recipients first (including status webhook flow).
5.  Validate retry and idempotency behavior under webhook failure simulation.

For error handling guidance, see [Meta API Error Reference](https://dualhook.com/docs/api-errors)
. For account health management, see [Maintain Account Health](https://dualhook.com/docs/account-health)
.

Related
-------

*   [Maintain Account Health](https://dualhook.com/docs/account-health)
    Ownership hygiene, quality monitoring, opt-out governance, and incident playbook.
*   [Messaging Webhook](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-webhook)
    Real-time webhook events for inbound messages, delivery statuses, and errors.
*   [Messaging Overview](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-overview)
    Core messaging endpoint, text messages, formatting, delivery statuses, and common errors.

# WhatsApp API Architecture & Security | Dualhook

Browse Docs

WhatsApp API Architecture & Security
====================================

Cloud API architecture, encryption, data residency, GDPR, and Dualhook's direct-routing security model.

Looking for the high-level overview first? Start with [WhatsApp API Privacy](https://dualhook.com/whatsapp-api-privacy)
 and then return here for the implementation details.

Cloud API Architecture[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#cloud-api-architecture)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Since October 2025, WhatsApp Business Platform runs on Cloud API. At a high level:

*   Businesses send messages through Meta Graph API
*   Businesses receive events through webhooks
*   Meta Cloud API acts as the managed messaging intermediary between business systems and WhatsApp transport

Encryption Model[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#encryption-model)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

WhatsApp messaging uses the Signal protocol for encryption. Cloud API also applies standard platform security controls:

*   **Data in transit** — `HTTPS` + `TLS`
*   **Data at rest** — encrypted storage on Meta infrastructure

Security boundary:

*   WhatsApp transport does not expose message content to WhatsApp operators.
*   Cloud API processes message content to provide platform functionality on behalf of the business.

Message Flow[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#message-flow)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

### User to Business[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#user-to-business)

1.  User sends a message.
2.  Message is encrypted in transit to Cloud API.
3.  Cloud API processes and decrypts for delivery to the business webhook.
4.  Data is temporarily retained for core platform functionality (e.g. retries and retransmissions).

### Business to User[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#business-to-user)

1.  Business sends message request to Cloud API.
2.  Cloud API temporarily stores and processes for delivery and reliability.
3.  Cloud API encrypts for destination delivery.
4.  WhatsApp transport delivers to the user client.

In Dualhook setups, inbound messages arrive at your endpoint directly from Meta via [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
. For outbound operations, your backend calls Dualhook's exact allowlisted Graph-compatible runtime routes with a per-connection `dh_live_...` key. The surface covers messages, media, selected templates, health/status, profiles, safe phone/calling settings, and QR codes without becoming an arbitrary Graph gateway.

All native authenticated Graph calls made by Dualhook pass through a server-only transport that derives Meta's app-secret proof from the exact authorizing token. Neither the token nor the proof is exposed to customers. The runtime resolves the existing authoritative routing projection before decrypting authorization, compares every route to the connection's stored phone/WABA assets, verifies template and media object ownership, rejects customer-controlled fields/hosts/callbacks, and uses manual redirect handling so credentials cannot be forwarded to another origin. OAuth code exchange (before a token exists), inbound webhook signatures, and validated Facebook/CDN media downloads are separate documented flows rather than Graph proof exceptions inferred by callers.

Local Storage (Data Residency)[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#local-storage-data-residency)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cloud API supports local storage for message data at rest in selected regions. This is useful for businesses with regulatory or residency requirements.

Data localized by Local Storage can include:

*   Incoming and outgoing messages
*   Text, media, and template payloads
*   Limited metadata needed for linkage and auditing

### Supported Regions (as of February 2026)[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#supported-regions-as-of-february-2026)

| Region | Countries |
| --- | --- |
| APAC | India, Singapore, Indonesia, South Korea, Japan, Australia |
| LATAM | Brazil |
| MEA | South Africa, Bahrain |
| Europe | EU (Germany), UK, Switzerland |
| North America | Canada |

Region availability can change. Always validate against current Meta documentation before rollout.

### Enabling Local Storage[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#enabling-local-storage)

1.  Request Local Storage for a specific [WABA](https://dualhook.com/docs/whatsapp-business-accounts)
     through support.
2.  Specify target storage region.
3.  Confirm change with the PIN sent to the WABA [phone number](https://dualhook.com/docs/phone-numbers)
    .
4.  Verify data location after activation.

Rollback to default region typically requires a support request as well.

Stored and Collected Data[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#stored-and-collected-data)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cloud API stores and processes operational data needed for platform behavior. Published guidance describes temporary message retention up to 30 days for core functionality (such as retries and retransmissions).

Business identity and config data is managed in Meta business systems. Consumer identifiers used for delivery are processed for message routing.

GDPR and Shared Responsibility[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#gdpr-and-shared-responsibility)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta provides platform controls and documentation to support compliance. Each business remains responsible for its own legal compliance obligations (GDPR and other applicable laws).

Platform security controls do not replace your internal privacy, access-control, and retention policies.

Dualhook Security Model[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#dualhook-security-model)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dualhook follows a stricter privacy boundary than what Cloud API requires:

*   Message content is routed directly from Meta to your webhook endpoint via [Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
    .
*   Inbound message-path webhooks go directly from Meta to your endpoint and are not proxied by Dualhook.
*   Outbound message and media payloads transit Dualhook's runtime without body persistence, caching, or content logging. Successful allowlisted phone/WABA metadata reads use a connection-isolated 60-second cache; message, media, template, profile, error, and mutation responses are never cached.
*   Meta tokens, app secrets, generated proofs, Authorization headers, and credential-bearing Meta URLs are excluded from logs, persisted errors, analytics, and customer responses.
*   Structured, quoted-JSON, and JSON-encoded error fields pass through the same credential sanitizer. The runtime preserves safe public Meta error fields while sanitizing non-success JSON before relay.
*   Management responses use explicit projections; SIP credentials, encryption material, storage settings, callback configuration, and raw pagination URLs are removed even if Meta returns them unexpectedly.
*   Customer-controlled webhook subscriptions or phone-level webhook overrides are not exposed. WABA routing and offboarding remain owned by Dualhook's existing lifecycle services.
*   Dualhook stores only operational metadata needed for setup, monitoring, and [compliance](https://dualhook.com/docs/compliance)
     features.

See [Compliance & Data Retention](https://dualhook.com/docs/compliance)
 for retention windows and export options.

Operational Security Checklist[](https://dualhook.com/docs/architecture-security#operational-security-checklist)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Protect each connection's `dh_live_...` key and rotate it from the connection Overview page. Dualhook does not expose its customer-scoped Meta authorization tokens.
*   Validate inbound webhook POSTs (envelope, WABA ID, `phone_number_id`), keep the override URL high-entropy and private, and enforce HTTPS. See [Messaging Webhook → Inbound Webhook POST Validation](https://dualhook.com/docs/messaging-webhook#signature-validation-post)
    .
*   Use least-privilege roles for [Meta portfolio](https://dualhook.com/docs/meta-business-portfolio)
     and system users.
*   Enable and manage [two-step verification](https://dualhook.com/docs/two-step-verification)
     on business numbers.
*   Monitor [quality](https://dualhook.com/docs/capacity-quality-limits)
    , account alerts, and security-related [webhook events](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-events)
    .
*   Keep clear audit trails for template changes, number ownership, and webhook endpoint changes.

Related
-------

*   [Compliance & Data Retention](https://dualhook.com/docs/compliance)
    Privacy boundary, configurable retention, CSV export, and organization isolation.
*   [WhatsApp Webhook Override](https://dualhook.com/docs/webhook-override)
    How Dualhook uses WhatsApp Webhook Override to route supported customer-path webhooks directly from Meta to your server.
